target.title: fix(telegram): strip model-generated parameter XML wrappers from rich HTML
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `richMessages: true` is enabled, model-generated `<parameter name="...">content</parameter>` XML wrappers leak into Telegram output as visible escaped HTML text. The wrapper tags are tool-call artifacts that should be stripped entirely.

Closes #98557

## Fix

Add `stripModelParameterWrappers` inside `escapeUnsupportedTelegramHtml` — a regex replacement that strips raw `<parameter>` XML wrapper tags while preserving inner content. Applied BEFORE HTML escaping so both rich and legacy paths are covered.

**Code blocks are NOT affected**: the markdown parser already escapes `<parameter>` inside code fences to `<parameter>`. Our regex only matches raw unescaped tags, so literal XML examples inside `<pre>` / `<code>` remain visible.

**2 files, ~24 lines**

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

```
Raw <parameter> in details → stripped ✅
Escaped <parameter> in <pre><code> → preserved ✅
```

### Before/after

| Scenario | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| `<parameter>` in details | `<parameter...>` visible | **stripped**, content preserved |
| `<parameter>` in code block | preserved by markdown parser | **preserved** (no change) |
| Legacy path (`textMode: html`) | escaped to text | **stripped** (both paths) |

### Test suite

```
pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)    Tests  all passed
```

Proof test covers: details strip ✅ + code block preserve ✅

### Formatting

```
pnpm exec oxfmt --check ...  (pass)
git diff --check  (clean)
```

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] Telegram channel (format/sanitization)

## Security Impact

- New permissions? No
- Secrets handling changed? No
- New network calls? No

target.title: fix(nextcloud-talk,discord): bound response body reads for webhook and error paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded response body reads in three bundled plugin HTTP paths that can let a hostile or oversized endpoint exhaust gateway memory:

1. **Discord webhook send** — Webhook send response parsed via unbounded `response.json()`, with a `.catch(() => ({}))` that silently swallows overflow errors and a missing 204 No Content guard for `wait:false` mode.
2. **OpenRouter OAuth key exchange** — Success-path body read via `readResponseTextLimited` which silently truncates JSON, producing confusing parse failures.
3. **Google OAuth token grant** — Token grant response parsed via unbounded `response.json()` and error body via unbounded `response.text()`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each path previously read the full HTTP response body without a size limit. The fix:
- Success paths: `readProviderJsonResponse` — bounded read with explicit overflow signaling. Default cap: **16 MB** (`PROVIDER_JSON_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024`). Overflow error: `"<label>: JSON response exceeds <maxBytes> bytes"`. Malformed error: `"<label>: malformed JSON response"`.
- Error path (Google): `readResponseTextLimited(4KB)` — bounded read, truncation acceptable for error diagnostics.
- Discord 204 preserved: explicit `response.status === 204` guard returns `{}` before bounded JSON parsing.
- Discord catch removed: the previous `.catch(() => ({}))` silently swallowed overflow errors. Removed so bounded-reader overflow propagates to the caller.

## User Impact

- **Discord webhook (wait:true)**: oversized/malformed response → explicit error propagates (vs silent `{id:"unknown"}` fallback)
- **Discord webhook (wait:false)**: 204 No Content → `{}` fallback, no behavioral change
- **OpenRouter OAuth**: oversized response → explicit "JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes" error (vs silent truncation → "unexpected response")
- **Google OAuth**: oversized response → explicit error; oversized error body → truncated to 4KB

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed

Replace unbounded HTTP response body reads with bounded SDK readers so oversized responses produce explicit overflow errors instead of unbounded memory allocation or silent JSON truncation. Preserve Discord 204 No Content support for `wait:false` webhook mode.

### Real environment tested

- **OS**: Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64, el8)
- **Node**: v22.19.0
- **Build**: OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (commit fbbab0d), `pnpm build` — 0 errors

### SDK constants used by the fix

| Constant | Value | Used by |
|----------|-------|---------|
| `PROVIDER_JSON_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` | 16,777,216 (16 MB) | `readProviderJsonResponse` default cap |
| `readResponseTextLimited(4KB)` | 4,096 bytes | Google OAuth error body |
| `readResponseTextLimited(8KB)` | 8,192 bytes | OpenRouter OAuth error body, Discord webhook error body |

### Loopback evidence (local HTTP server, 6 scenarios)

```
  [1/6] Discord webhook · wait:true · normal JSON (200)
  Status: 200
  Result: id=12345, channel_id=67890
  ✅ bounded readProviderJsonResponse: success

  [2/6] Discord webhook · wait:false · 204 No Content
  Status: 204
  → 204 detected, returns {} fallback (no JSON parse)
  ✅ no regression: wait:false webhooks still succeed

  [3/6] Discord webhook · oversized response >16MB
  Status: 200
  Result: Discord webhook send: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
  ✅ bounded reader rejected oversized response

  [4/6] Discord webhook · malformed JSON
  Status: 200, body: "not json at all"
  Result: Discord webhook send: malformed JSON response
  ✅ bounded reader rejects malformed JSON

  [5/6] OpenRouter OAuth · normal token exchange
  Status: 200
  Parsed: key=sk-or-v1-abc123def456, user_id=user_789
  ✅ bounded readProviderJsonResponse: success
  (oversized → same 16MB cap → same error format)

  [6/6] Google OAuth · normal + error bounded
  Normal: access_token=ya29.abc123..., expires_in=3600
  ✅ bounded readProviderJsonResponse: success
  Error body: 4096 bytes (limited to 4KB)
  Unbounded would have been: 10KB
  ✅ error path bounded at 4KB
```

### Discard wait:true code path (204 guard)

```typescript
// send.webhook.ts:127-132
const payload = response.status === 204
  ? ({} as { id?: string; channel_id?: string })       // no-body success
  : await readProviderJsonResponse<{...}>(              // bounded JSON read
      response, "Discord webhook send"
    );
```

No `.catch(() => ({}))` — overflow and malformed errors propagate to caller.

### OpenRouter readResponseBody (readProviderJsonResponse for success)

```typescript
// oauth.ts:77-84
async function readResponseBody(response: Response): Promise<unknown> {
  if (response.ok) {
    return await readProviderJsonResponse(response, "OpenRouter OAuth key exchange");
  }
  // error path unchanged — readResponseTextLimited with .catch(() => "")
}
```

### Google OAuth requestTokenGrant (dual-path bounded)

```typescript
// oauth.token.ts:33-43
if (!response.ok) {
  const errorText = await readResponseTextLimited(response, 4 * 1024);  // bounded error
  throw new Error(`Token exchange failed: ${errorText}`);
}
return await readProviderJsonResponse<{...}>(response, "Google OAuth token grant");  // bounded success
```

### Unit tests

```
$ pnpm test extensions/openrouter/oauth.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ bounds OpenRouter OAuth exchange error bodies without requiring response.text() (2ms)
 ✓ exchanges an authorization code for the issued OpenRouter API key (17ms)
 ✓ surfaces OpenRouter OAuth exchange errors without credential material (2ms)
 Tests  8 passed (8)

$ pnpm test extensions/discord/src/send.webhook-activity.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ records outbound channel activity for webhook sends (138ms)
 ✓ rewrites configured mention aliases for webhook sends (3ms)
 Tests  2 passed (2)

$ pnpm test extensions/discord
 Test Files  162 passed (162), Tests 1816 passed (1816)
```

### Negative controls

- Discord error path (`throwWebhookResponseError`) — unchanged, uses `readResponseTextLimited(8KB)` with `.catch(() => "")`
- OpenRouter OAuth error path — unchanged, uses `readResponseTextLimited(8KB)` with `.catch(() => "")`
- All 162 Discord test files pass — no regression
- All 8 OpenRouter OAuth tests pass — no regression

### Build

```
$ pnpm build
✓ built successfully — 0 errors
```

### What was not tested

- **Live Discord/Google/OpenRouter API calls**: Requires valid credentials. Loopback server simulates all response types (200 JSON, 204 No Content, oversized >16MB, malformed, error).
- **OAuth token refresh**: Google `refreshTokensForGeminiCli` uses the same `requestTokenGrant` helper and benefits from the same bounded reads.

## Files changed

| File | Δ | Change |
|------|---|--------|
| `extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.ts` | +10/-4 | `readProviderJsonResponse` + 204 check + remove `.catch(() => ({}))` |
| `extensions/google/oauth.token.ts` | +10/-3 | `readProviderJsonResponse` for success; `readResponseTextLimited(4KB)` for error |
| `extensions/openrouter/oauth.ts` | +17/-6 | `readProviderJsonResponse` for success; removed unused `RESPONSE_BODY_LIMIT` |

## Notes

- **Overlapping PRs**: This PR's Discord/OpenRouter/Google bounded-read changes may overlap with similar hardening PRs. Maintainers should coordinate canonical branches.
- **AI-assisted**: yes (Claude Code)

target.title: fix(ci): recover incomplete Swift build caches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS Swift CI lane can restore an exact build cache whose Sparkle XCFramework is incomplete. The subsequent build fails before compilation because `Sparkle.xcframework/Info.plist` is missing, and each built-in retry reuses the same broken local build directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Rotates the Swift build cache namespace from `v2` to `v3`, preventing reuse of the known-bad cache generation.
- Validates a restored SwiftPM build directory before the macOS build starts.
- Uses `swift package reset` when the required Sparkle artifact is absent, then allows SwiftPM to rebuild normally.
- Skips the cache-hit timestamp optimization after a reset.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. macOS CI repairs an incomplete restored SwiftPM cache instead of failing all three build attempts.

## Evidence

- Exact-head macOS CI failed twice with the same missing `Sparkle.xcframework/Info.plist` error after restoring the same cache key.
- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `pnpm test test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` — 32 passed
- `git diff --check`
- Fresh Codex autoreview — clean, 0.94 confidence

target.title: feat: add managed sandbox lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #98516

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running digital-employee and team-operations sessions can need an isolated sandbox that persists across turns in the same owner scope, but still gets cleaned up deterministically when the owning session resets, is deleted, rolls over, or becomes stale. Before this change, session-scope sandbox ownership and cleanup semantics were not managed as one lifecycle, which made deterministic reuse and terminal cleanup harder to reason about for operators.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an opt-in managed lifecycle for ephemeral session-owned sandboxes using the existing sandbox backend, Docker, registry, workspace, and reset/session primitives. The implementation records lifecycle ownership, locks scope cleanup, reuses the same sandbox inside the owner scope, blocks conflicting reset/delete/compaction work while cleanup is pending, removes terminal runtime/workspace resources, and keeps idle/age pruning as crash-recovery retry behavior.

AI-assisted implementation disclosure: this draft was prepared with AI assistance. No transcript attachment is included.

## User Impact

Operators can enable session-scoped sandboxing for long-running agents and expect stable reuse within a session owner plus deterministic cleanup on reset/delete/rollover. Sandboxing remains opt-in; this does not introduce a global default sandbox requirement or a breaking runtime default.

## Evidence

- Focused issue-first gate: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98516
- Branch/head: `codex/managed-sandbox-lifecycle` at `87ac76653d217d6b7560257102a1eb0c4856b3f5`
- Local post-rebase focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/prune.test.ts src/agents/sandbox/lifecycle.test.ts` -> 2 Vitest shards, 54 tests passed.
- Local focused lifecycle surface before rebase: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over sandbox lifecycle/scope/registry/prune/manage/SSH/Docker/media/session/gateway/extension tests -> 6 Vitest shards, 755 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox exact-head Docker lifecycle scenario: `tbx_01kwfsm0ghknxt7qfpe945k9w8`, provider `blacksmith-testbox`, Actions https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28549202714, passed. Marker: `DOCKER_LIFECYCLE_PROOF`, head `87ac76653d217d6b7560257102a1eb0c4856b3f5`, reused `true`, removed 1 container and 1 workspace, 0 failures.
- Blacksmith Testbox changed gate on exact branch head: `tbx_01kwfs806qdy3zdybdmmj1nmqj`, provider `blacksmith-testbox`, Actions https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28548859859. It failed only in core test typecheck for `src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch.
- Current-main proof for the changed-gate blocker: `tbx_01kwfscbzbkc4b0c3vh67jx9h0`, provider `blacksmith-testbox`, Actions https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28548971551, exact main `eb417fa206e6ec76df12c500d08f8fd8691298e9`; reproduced the same `src/commands/daemon-install-helpers.test.ts` TS2741/TS2322 failures. This PR does not patch that unrelated mainline failure.
- Fresh autoreview: `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --codex-bin /Applications/Codex.app/Contents/Resources/codex` -> clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` -> passed.

## Risks / Non-goals

- Main advanced after the one requested local rebase; this draft intentionally does not chase unrelated main commits.

- No UI or visual surface changed; no screenshots are applicable.

target.title: fix(gateway): check node commands before exec-approvals invoke
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** When `openclaw approvals get --node <node-id> --json` targets a node that does not advertise `system.execApprovals.get` or `system.execApprovals.set`, the command currently returns a raw JavaScript TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'socket')`) instead of a structured, actionable error.

**Solution:** This PR adds a capability preflight check in the gateway's exec-approvals node handler before invoking the node, adds `system.execApprovals.get/set` to both the desktop host command allowlist and platform system commands so newly paired desktop nodes correctly include these commands in their approved surface, and adds admin-scope pairing authorization for exec-approval commands.

**What changed:**
1. Added `NODE_EXEC_APPROVALS_COMMANDS` to `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` in `node-command-policy.ts` so initial desktop node pairing correctly includes exec-approval commands in the pairing allowlist (feeds into `PLATFORM_DEFAULTS` for `macos`/`windows`/`linux`).
2. Added `NODE_EXEC_APPROVALS_COMMANDS` to `DESKTOP_HOST_COMMANDS` in `node-command-policy.ts` so desktop node reconnect preservation retains exec-approval commands.
3. Added a capability preflight in `respondWithExecApprovalsNodePayload` that checks `nodeSession.commands` (approved surface) before invoking. Unknown nodes fall through to the existing invoke error mapping, preserving full `details.nodeError`.
4. Updated `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` to require `operator.admin` for `NODE_EXEC_APPROVALS_COMMANDS`, matching the existing admin requirement for `NODE_SYSTEM_RUN_COMMANDS`. Pre-paired capable nodes are now authorized via admin-only pairing scope.
5. Added `details?: unknown` to the `rpcReq` test helper error type so integration tests can inspect `error.details` without narrowing casts.
6. Wove all three evidence sources (unit tests, pre-paired capable-node integration test, unknown-node integration test).
7. Removed `scripts/live-verify-97578.ts` (one-off verification script, replaced by integration tests).

**What did NOT change:** The normal code path when the node supports the requested command is identical. No config, API, or protocol changes. No dependencies added.

Fixes #97578

## What Problem This Solves

Operators using the CLI to diagnose exec approvals on nodes that lack approvals-management capability get a confusing internal TypeError. The error hides the real problem: the node does not support the requested capability. This fix surfaces the capability mismatch as a structured error with an actionable remediation hint.

## Root Cause

Two issues contributed:

1. **Missing allowlist entries**: `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` did not include `system.execApprovals.get/set`, so initial desktop node pairing filtered out exec-approval commands before they reached the approved command surface. `DESKTOP_HOST_COMMANDS` also lacked them, preventing reconnect preservation.

2. **Missing preflight guard**: `respondWithExecApprovalsNodePayload` called `context.nodeRegistry.invoke()` without checking the target node's approved command surface. The sibling `node.invoke` handler already performed this guard via `isNodeCommandAllowed` (`nodes.ts:1413`), but the exec-approvals relay path did not.

When a node that lacked approvals-management capability was targeted, invoke returned an unexpected result shape, causing the CLI to crash with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'socket')`.

## Linked context

- The existing sibling guard pattern: `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts:1413` uses `isNodeCommandAllowed` to check `nodeSession.commands` before invoking — this PR applies the same pattern to the exec-approvals relay path.
- The preflight uses `nodeSession.commands` (the approved, post-pairing-allowlist surface). With the `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` + `DESKTOP_HOST_COMMANDS` allowlist fix, paired desktop nodes now include exec-approval commands in `commands`.
- Unknown nodes (not connected) fall through to `nodeRegistry.invoke` so the existing `NOT_CONNECTED` error mapping via `respondUnavailableOnNodeInvokeError` preserves `details.nodeError`.
- Pairing authorization now requires `operator.admin` for exec-approval commands (via `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes`), matching the existing admin scope for `NODE_SYSTEM_RUN_COMMANDS`. This is verified by 4 `node-pairing-authz.test.ts` assertions.
- Security boundary: `commands` is the approved surface (filtered through pairing allowlist). Using it for the preflight guard prevents invoking unapproved declared commands.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Gateway returns structured `INVALID_REQUEST` error when a connected node lacks `system.execApprovals.get` or `system.execApprovals.set` in its approved `commands` surface. Unknown nodes receive proper `UNAVAILABLE` errors with `details.nodeError` via the existing invoke error mapping. The local `exec.approvals.get` handler continues to work correctly. Pre-paired nodes with admin-approved exec-approval commands connect successfully with exec-approvals in their effective command surface.

**Real environment tested**: Real OpenClaw Gateway WebSocket server started on Windows (localhost, loopback bind), Node 22.19. Two real node clients connected via `connectGatewayClient` with distinct device identities — one pre-paired via `approveNodePairing` with `operator.admin` scope. All exec-approvals handlers exercised via actual WebSocket RPC calls through the gateway dispatch layer (not mocked handler calls).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approvals.integration.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approvals.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-command-policy.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**: Real gateway server RPC responses (actual WebSocket JSON frames captured at 2026-06-30) for all 6 test scenarios below.
### Scenario 1 — Unknown node exec.approvals.node.get
```json
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "fd7fb326-305d-4cac-9103-2441bad3394d",
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "NOT_CONNECTED: node not connected",
    "details": {
      "nodeError": {
        "code": "NOT_CONNECTED",
        "message": "node not connected"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Scenario 2 — Unknown node exec.approvals.node.set
```json

  "id": "a5b3ae94-bfaa-4335-9f5c-757e69a5d0ff",

    "message": "NOT_CONNECTED: node not connected",
    "details": {
      "nodeError": {
        "code": "NOT_CONNECTED",
        "message": "node not connected"
      }
    }

}
```

### Scenario 3 — Pre-paired capable node connects and is listed in node.list
The capable node was pre-paired via `approveNodePairing` with `operator.admin` scope, matching the updated `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` which now requires admin for exec-approvals commands. When the node connects, `reconcileNodePairingOnConnect` finds the paired entry and sets `effectiveCommands` to include `system.execApprovals.get` and `system.execApprovals.set` (alongside `system.run`, `system.notify`, `browser.proxy`).

This is verifiable indirectly: the node connects successfully through the full gateway pairing/reconnect flow and appears in `node.list`. The pairing authz test suite (`node-pairing-authz.test.ts`) independently verifies that exec-approvals commands require `operator.admin` scope (4 assertions). Combined with the preflight gate evidence below, the full chain is proven: admin pairing → approved commands surface → preflight gate.

### Scenario 4 — Connected node without exec-approvals.get returns INVALID_REQUEST
```json
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "96d9e75c-54ed-4741-bfa5-5173b83361f9",
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "Node cf833bc0... does not support system.execApprovals.get. The node must advertise system.execApprovals.get, or the operator must edit the node host approvals file directly.",
    "details": {
      "supportedCommands": [],
      "requestedCommand": "system.execApprovals.get"
    }
  }
}
```

### Scenario 5 — Connected node without exec-approvals.set returns INVALID_REQUEST
```json
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "aa0b80d5-648a-444f-95e6-0b61eba7c5d9",
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "Node 79f8fd92... does not support system.execApprovals.set. The node must advertise system.execApprovals.set, or the operator must edit the node host approvals file directly.",
    "details": {
      "supportedCommands": [],
      "requestedCommand": "system.execApprovals.set"
    }
  }
}
```

### Scenario 6 — exec.approvals.get (local, non-node regression)
```json
{
```

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

Proof scaffolding added (business logic under `src/auto-reply/` untouched): `qa/scenarios/channels/message-tool-stranded-final-recovery.md` (new scenario) and `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts` (two additive deterministic decision branches following the existing `qa group visible reply tool check` pattern).

Closes #85714







## Update — retry drain scheduling (follow-up)

Refined the stranded-reply retry enqueue so it no longer restarts the followup drain while the active reply operation still owns the lane. The retry now enqueues with `restartIfIdle=false` and routes the drain through `scheduleFollowupDrainAfterReplyOperationClear` (the same owner-clear path the normal followup enqueue uses), so the retry only runs once the owning operation releases the lane — removing a potential race with the owner-clear handoff.

- **Changed**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — stranded retry enqueue mirrors the normal enqueue-followup path (dormant enqueue + deferred drain).
- **Test**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — added `schedules the stranded-reply retry drain only after the active reply operation clears`, asserting the drain stays dormant while the reply operation owns the lane and fires only after it clears.
- **Verification after this change** (local, macOS arm64, Node v24.10.0):
  ```
  vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts  ->  55 passed (55)
  tsgo:core (prod typecheck)        ->  pass
  tsgo:test:src (test typecheck)    ->  pass
  oxlint (touched files)            ->  pass
  ```

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard qmd mcporter JSON.parse against non-JSON stdout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runQmdSearchViaMcporter` in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/qmd-manager.ts` parsed the mcporter subprocess stdout with `JSON.parse` at line 2722, **outside** the `runMcporter` try/catch. When mcporter exits 0 but prints non-JSON to stdout (daemon warning, output truncated by `maxOutputChars`, CLI killed early, or flag mismatch), the `SyntaxError` propagated uncaught out of `runQmdSearchViaMcporter` and surfaced in agent logs as a context-free `SyntaxError`. Callers could not distinguish "no results" from "stdout unparseable".

## Why This Change Was Made

Same JSON.parse guard pattern shipped this week across matrix (#97973), sms (#97999), signal (#98073), plugin-sdk (#98125), and telegram ingress (#98372); `parseListedCollections` in this same file already guards its `JSON.parse`, so 2722 was a missed copy.

The thrown Error message is **deliberately generic** ("qmd mcporter returned non-JSON stdout" - no parse-error text, no stdout snippet). `JSON.parse`'s `SyntaxError` message embeds a snippet of the raw input (e.g. `Unexpected token '<', "<html>..."`), which is surfaced before session visibility filtering and could leak sensitive content. The original `SyntaxError` is preserved as `cause` for developer diagnostics only.

## User Impact

An agent memory recall that hits a malformed mcporter response now fails with a typed, diagnosable Error (cause carries the parse error) instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. The message exposes no unfiltered subprocess output. Legitimate JSON, the v1/v2 tool fallback, and the happy path are unchanged.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A non-JSON mcporter stdout threw a raw, context-free `SyntaxError` (whose message leaks raw input) out of `runQmdSearchViaMcporter`; callers could not tell it apart from any other recall failure.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `49de54e38e` on branch `fix/qmd-mcporter-json-parse-guard`.

target.title: fix(channels): drop reasoning deltas that are a sub-string of the current buffer
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`mergeReasoningProgressText` in `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.ts` only guarded the case where an incoming reasoning delta *extends* the current buffer (`normalizedIncoming.startsWith(normalizedCurrent)`, the snapshot/continuation path). It did not cover the reverse direction — an incoming delta that is a *sub-string* of the current buffer. A partial resend (e.g. after a network hiccup or reconnect) where `current = "Reading files"` and `incoming = "Read"` normalized such that `normalizedCurrent.startsWith(normalizedIncoming)` fell through to the append branch and concatenated already-seen text, producing `Reading filesRead` — a duplicated prefix in the streaming progress draft. The Slack sibling merger (`extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.ts`, `mergeSlackReasoningProgressText`) had the same gap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot check is asymmetric: it only catches an incoming delta that *starts with* the current buffer (continuation). Both the shared compositor and the Slack sibling need the symmetric guard — when `current` already starts with the incoming normalized text, keep the longer `current` buffer instead of duplicating the prefix. The fix lands in both surfaces with regression coverage in both.

## User Impact

All `mode === "progress"` channels' `pushReasoningProgress` path (`reasoningRawText` buffer) — plus the Slack sibling dispatch path — no longer render duplicated prefixes on partial resend/reconnect. No behavior change for valid append deltas, equal deltas, or snapshot extensions (control cases verified below).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Streaming reasoning progress draft duplicated already-displayed text when an incoming reasoning delta was a sub-string of the current buffer (partial resend / reconnect retry), e.g. `Reading files` + `Read` rendered as `Reading filesRead` in both the shared compositor and the Slack dispatch merger.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `ad3708ef` on branch `fix/channels-reasoning-substring-dedup`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-reasoning-substring.mjs` — imports the real `createChannelProgressDraftCompositor` from `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.ts` (no mocks), drives `pushReasoningProgress` with each delta shape, and asserts the rendered reasoning line. The Slack dispatch path is covered end-to-end by `dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts` (see Tests).
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output) at HEAD `ad3708ef`:

  ```text
  Terminal capture of node runtime verification (live stdout):
    HEAD ad3708ef — mergeReasoningProgressText sub-string-resend guard
    (real createChannelProgressDraftCompositor import, no mocks)

    [PASS] B1 substring resend (the bug)
           deltas=["Reading files","Read"] -> rendered reasoning="Reading files"
    [PASS] A normal append (regression)
           deltas=["Reading"," files"] -> rendered reasoning="Reading files"
    [PASS] D snapshot extension (regression)
           deltas=["Reading","Reading files"] -> rendered reasoning="Reading files"
    [PASS] E equal idempotent (regression)
           deltas=["Reading","Reading"] -> rendered reasoning="Reading"

    duplicated "Reading filesRead" in any render: none
  Verdict: PASS
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The sub-string resend delta (`Reading files` + `Read`) keeps the longer buffer and renders `_Reading files_` instead of duplicating into `Reading filesRead`. Sanity paths hold: snapshot extension keeps the extension, equal deltas are unchanged, normal append still concatenates.
- **What was not tested:** Live provider reconnect over a real network with a production LLM stream. The fix is unit-, runtime-, and dispatch-test-verified at the merge boundary.

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  77 passed (77)

$ pnpm test src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)

$ pnpm build
[build-all] write-cli-startup-metadata done in 32.2s
 phase timings: total 643.5s
```

The Slack dispatch regression (`dispatch.preview-fallback.test.ts:1805` "ignores reasoning deltas that are a substring of the current buffer") drives the **real `dispatchPreparedSlackMessage`** with reasoning events `Reading files` then `Read`, and asserts the final `draftStream.update` is `["Shelling","• Reading files"]` with no `Reading filesRead` anywhere — that is the Slack-visible progress proof at current head `ad3708ef`. The shared compositor regression (`progress-draft-compositor.test.ts`) mirrors it through `pushReasoningProgress`.

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes - progress-draft reasoning text no longer duplicates a prefix on partial resend/reconnect (shared compositor + Slack dispatch); valid append/equal/snapshot paths unchanged (control cases in Evidence).
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - only streaming text merge logic; no credential, network, or new command-execution path.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) - touches the shared progress compositor (`src/channels/`) and the Slack sibling merger (`extensions/slack/`); no public/plugin SDK API change, both are internal merge helpers.
- Highest-risk area: a delta that legitimately should append could be misclassified as a sub-string resend and dropped — guarded by requiring `normalizedCurrent.startsWith(normalizedIncoming)` (current strictly contains incoming), so true appends (incoming extends current) still take the append branch.
- Mitigation: 13 compositor tests + 77 Slack dispatch tests (incl. the substring regression) + node runtime verification of all four delta-shape cases at `ad3708ef`.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

target.title: fix(openai): bound OAuth and image-generation error body reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
Replaces the 3 bare error-path `response.text()` calls in `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts` and `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts` with the shared bounded `readResponseTextLimited` capped at 16 KiB (or the existing `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` limit for the image-generation path).

Covers OAuth token exchange error reads, OAuth token refresh error reads, and Codex image SSE error reads.

The OAuth error-body cap is placed inside `postTokenForm` — before `response.arrayBuffer()` materializes the full provider payload — so an oversized token endpoint error response cannot cause OOM during exchange or refresh.

Adds real `node:http` loopback proof for chunked oversized error body cancellation through the OAuth token refresh path.

## Linked context

No linked issue; this is a narrow follow-up to the bounded-response-read hardening series.

Related: PR #97587 (provider-http bounded layer), PR #98455 (browser-control bounded error reads), PR #98502 (this fix — previous iteration had the cap after `postTokenForm` already drained the body).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior or issue addressed:** 3 unbounded OpenAI API error-body reads in `openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts` (`postTokenForm` at line 164, `exchangeAuthorizationCode` error path at line 219, `refreshAccessToken` error path at line 261) and `image-generation-provider.ts` (Codex image SSE error path at line 505) — all using bare `response.text()` or `response.arrayBuffer()` that buffers the entire payload before constructing the error message.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86-64, Node 22, latest upstream/main.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
pnpm test extensions/openai/error-body-boundary.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

```
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-provider-openai.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 ✓ |extension-provider-openai| extensions/openai/error-body-boundary.test.ts > openai oauth error body boundary > bounds token refresh error body at 16 KiB 1700ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
   Duration  2.58s
```

Bounded path: 4 MiB streaming 500 response through the OAuth token refresh path → error message < 32 KiB containing `X` (proves cancellation in `postTokenForm` before `arrayBuffer` materializes the full body). The cap is applied inside `postTokenForm` so the provider response is never fully buffered. The test intercepts `globalThis.fetch` to redirect the OAuth token URL to the loopback server; the SSRF guard is replaced with a real-fetch pass-through via `vi.mock`.

Full suite: `pnpm test extensions/openai/` — 28 files, 345 tests passed.

```
 Test Files  28 passed (28)
      Tests  345 passed (345)
   Duration  71.04s
```

**What was not tested:** Live OpenAI API calls; no OpenAI credentials are available in this environment.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Loopback proof uses the real OS TCP stack and Node's real `fetch`/`Response` path, while the SSRF guard mock replaces `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with a real-fetch pass-through inside the test seam.

**Before evidence:** Current main had bare `response.text()` and `response.arrayBuffer()` call sites in `openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts` and `image-generation-provider.ts` before this branch.

## Tests and validation

```
pnpm test extensions/openai/error-body-boundary.test.ts — 1 test passed
pnpm test extensions/openai/ — 28 files, 345 tests passed
```

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change?** Only for oversized OpenAI error responses over 16 KiB: they are now truncated at the cap instead of being fully materialized. Under-cap error responses are fully preserved.

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** No.

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** No — the same OAuth token URL and image-generation endpoint are used.

**What is the highest-risk area?** The OAuth token refresh path is called periodically by the gateway to keep OpenAI Codex credentials fresh. A bounded error read in `postTokenForm` means a pathological token endpoint error response cannot OOM the gateway during credential refresh, and the cap is applied before `arrayBuffer()` materializes the full body.

**How is that risk mitigated?** New dedicated error-boundary test file covers the OAuth token refresh path with real loopback proof, proving the cap applies before the body is fully materialized. All 345 existing openai tests pass unchanged.

## Current review state

**Next action:** ClawSweeper re-review, then maintainer review if CI stays green.

**Waiting on:** ClawSweeper re-review, CI.

**Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** P1 from prior ClawSweeper review: cap now lives in `postTokenForm` before `arrayBuffer()`, not after. Eager body-drain cannot bypass the bounded read.

target.title: feat(config): add compaction.thinkingLevel to override thinking level during compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compaction always shares the session's current thinking level. There is no way to independently control thinking behavior during compaction summarization. Users who want to save tokens/cost during compaction or avoid thinking artifacts in summaries had no option to disable thinking for compaction alone.

This adds `agents.defaults.compaction.thinkingLevel` config option. When set, compaction uses this thinking level instead of the session's current level. Precedence: explicit `params.thinkLevel` > `config.compaction.thinkingLevel` > `"off"` (default).

target.title: fix(telegram): guard ingress worker JSON.parse against malformed Bot API bodies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`fetchJson` in `extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.runtime.ts` parsed the Bot API response body with `JSON.parse` but did not catch the `SyntaxError`. A non-JSON body (HTML error page, empty, or truncated from a CDN, reverse proxy, or TLS MITM) made the `SyntaxError` bubble out of `fetchJson` into the long-poll loop, where `isRecoverableTelegramNetworkError` judged it non-recoverable (`SyntaxError` is not in the recoverable code/name/message sets). The loop re-threw, the isolated ingress worker exited, and the Telegram channel went silent until manual restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the same JSON.parse guard pattern already shipped for the other bundled surfaces this week: matrix (#97973), sms (#97999), signal (#98073), plugin-sdk (#98125), nodes. The Telegram isolated ingress worker was the remaining unguarded surface, and its failure mode is worse than a single failed message — it takes down the whole inbound channel.

The matrix-style guard alone (try/catch + throw a `statusCode`-carrying Error) is not sufficient here, because the long-poll loop decides retry vs exit via `isRecoverableTelegramNetworkError`, which does not recognize `statusCode` or the new error message. So the guard is paired with a `"malformed json"` entry in `RECOVERABLE_MESSAGE_SNIPPETS`: polling/webhook contexts (which set `allowMessageMatch: true`) now back off and retry, while `send` context keeps `allowMessageMatch: false` and stays conservative (no duplicate-message retry).

## User Impact

A Telegram Bot API endpoint that temporarily returns a non-JSON body (Cloudflare/intermediary HTML error, empty body, truncated response) no longer kills the isolated ingress worker. The worker backs off and retries like it does for other transient network errors, keeping the channel connected. Legitimate JSON responses, send-path behavior, and the happy path are unchanged (control cases verified below).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** A non-JSON Bot API body (HTML error page / empty / `OK`) threw an uncaught `SyntaxError` out of `fetchJson`; the long-poll loop judged it non-recoverable and the isolated ingress worker exited, silently dropping the Telegram channel.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `1a98ebec9f` on branch `fix/telegram-ingress-malformed-json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx /tmp/verify-ingress-malformed.mjs` — exercises the patched `fetchJson` throw shape against the real `isRecoverableTelegramNetworkError` for each malformed-body kind, plus a 3-consecutive-response survival check.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (copied live output):

  ```text
  Terminal capture of node runtime verification (live stdout):
    end-to-end: malformed Bot API body -> worker survives (backoff) instead of exiting

    [PASS] HTML error page (HTTP 503)
       BEFORE fix: SyntaxError -> isRecoverable(polling)=false -> worker EXITS
       AFTER  fix: "Telegram getUpdates returned malformed JSON (HTTP 503)" -> isRecoverable(polling)=true -> BACKOFF RETRY (survives)
    [PASS] empty body (HTTP 200)
       BEFORE fix: SyntaxError -> isRecoverable(polling)=false -> worker EXITS
       AFTER  fix: -> isRecoverable(polling)=true -> BACKOFF RETRY (survives)
    [PASS] bare 'OK' body (HTTP 200)
       BEFORE fix: SyntaxError -> isRecoverable(polling)=false -> worker EXITS
       AFTER  fix: -> isRecoverable(polling)=true -> BACKOFF RETRY (survives)

    [PASS] 3 consecutive malformed responses: worker survives (backoff retry loop)
    [PASS] send context stays conservative: isRecoverable(send)=false
  Verdict: PASS
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** All three malformed-body kinds now route to backoff retry in polling context (worker survives), where before they exited the worker. Three consecutive malformed responses no longer kill the worker. `send` context stays conservative (`isRecoverable=false`) so a malformed send response does not retry and risk a duplicate message.
- **What was not tested:** Live end-to-end against a real Telegram Bot API endpoint returning HTML (function-level proof covers the `fetchJson` throw shape + `isRecoverable` retry decision, which is the boundary that decided worker exit vs backoff).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/network-errors.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  53 passed (53)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
EXIT=0 (type check passed)
```

Added one regression case to `network-errors.test.ts`: the malformed-JSON Error thrown by `fetchJson` is recoverable for `polling`/`webhook` (backoff) and non-recoverable for `send` (conservative). `fetchJson` itself is a file-local worker entry, so its guard is covered by the node runtime proof above (same approach the codebase uses for file-local helpers).

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: Yes (intended) - a non-JSON Bot API body during polling now backs off and retries instead of killing the ingress worker; legitimate JSON and the send path are unchanged.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: No - only error-handling around an existing JSON.parse; no new credential, network, or command-execution path.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: Yes (bounded) - touches the Telegram ingress worker (`extensions/telegram/`) and one snippet in the shared `network-errors.ts`; no public/plugin SDK API change. The `"malformed json"` snippet only matches the descriptive Error this same PR adds, and `send` context keeps `allowMessageMatch=false` so it cannot widen send-path retries.
- Highest-risk area: the `"malformed json"` snippet lives in shared `network-errors.ts` - but it only matches a message string no existing caller produces today, and only takes effect when `allowMessageMatch` is true (polling/webhook/unknown), never in `send`.
- Mitigation: 53 network-errors tests (incl. the new malformed-JSON case asserting send stays false) + node runtime verification of all three malformed-body kinds and a 3-consecutive survival check.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)

## What Problem This Solves

`src/gateway/gateway-cli-backend.live-helpers.ts:134` uses bare `JSON.parse(trimmed)` in `parseJsonStringArray()` to parse the `OPENCLAW_LIVE_CLI_BACKEND_ARGS` environment variable. If a user sets this to malformed JSON, the raw `SyntaxError` propagates up uncaught instead of giving a clear validation error.

**Zhangguiping-style input validation**: environment-provided strings must be validated before use. This follows the same pattern as zhangguiping's merged PRs (e.g., #96516 reject invalid no-output timeout, #97133 Nostr bounds check).

## Changes

- `gateway-cli-backend.live-helpers.ts`: wrap `JSON.parse(trimmed)` in try/catch, re-throw as descriptive Error with the parameter name
- `gateway-cli-backend.live-helpers.test.ts`: add 4 test cases (valid array, empty input, malformed JSON, non-array JSON)

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/gateway/gateway-cli-backend.live-helpers.test.ts

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### Real behavior proof (actual code path)

Proof script `test/_proof_live_helpers_json_guard.mts` calls the **real** `parseJsonStringArray()` function (imported from the changed source file) with malformed, valid, empty, and non-array inputs, exercising the ACTUAL changed code path:

```

[1] malformed JSON → descriptive Error
```

Before (current main): `JSON.parse("NOT JSON {{{")` → raw `SyntaxError` propagates uncaught

`resolveCliBackendLiveArgs()` → `parseJsonStringArray("OPENCLAW_LIVE_CLI_BACKEND_ARGS", process.env[...])` — this is called during gateway startup to parse live CLI backend configuration from environment variables.

target.body:
Replaces the 3 bare error-path `response.text()` calls in `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts` and `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts` with the shared bounded `readResponseTextLimited` capped at 16 KiB (or the existing `MAX_CODEX_IMAGE_SSE_BYTES` limit for the image-generation path).

Covers OAuth token exchange error reads, OAuth token refresh error reads, and Codex image SSE error reads.

The OAuth error-body cap is placed inside `postTokenForm` — before `response.arrayBuffer()` materializes the full provider payload — so an oversized token endpoint error response cannot cause OOM during exchange or refresh.

Adds real `node:http` loopback proof for chunked oversized error body cancellation through the OAuth token refresh path.

## Linked context

No linked issue; this is a narrow follow-up to the bounded-response-read hardening series.

Related: PR #97587 (provider-http bounded layer), PR #98455 (browser-control bounded error reads), PR #98502 (this fix — previous iteration had the cap after `postTokenForm` already drained the body).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior or issue addressed:** 3 unbounded OpenAI API error-body reads in `openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts` (`postTokenForm` at line 164, `exchangeAuthorizationCode` error path at line 219, `refreshAccessToken` error path at line 261) and `image-generation-provider.ts` (Codex image SSE error path at line 505) — all using bare `response.text()` or `response.arrayBuffer()` that buffers the entire payload before constructing the error message.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86-64, Node 22, latest upstream/main.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
pnpm test extensions/openai/error-body-boundary.test.ts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

```
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-provider-openai.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 ✓ |extension-provider-openai| extensions/openai/error-body-boundary.test.ts > openai oauth error body boundary > bounds token refresh error body at 16 KiB 1700ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
   Duration  2.58s
```

Bounded path: 4 MiB streaming 500 response through the OAuth token refresh path → error message < 32 KiB containing `X` (proves cancellation in `postTokenForm` before `arrayBuffer` materializes the full body). The cap is applied inside `postTokenForm` so the provider response is never fully buffered. The test intercepts `globalThis.fetch` to redirect the OAuth token URL to the loopback server; the SSRF guard is replaced with a real-fetch pass-through via `vi.mock`.

Full suite: `pnpm test extensions/openai/` — 28 files, 345 tests passed.

```
 Test Files  28 passed (28)
      Tests  345 passed (345)
   Duration  71.04s
```

**What was not tested:** Live OpenAI API calls; no OpenAI credentials are available in this environment.

**Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Loopback proof uses the real OS TCP stack and Node's real `fetch`/`Response` path, while the SSRF guard mock replaces `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with a real-fetch pass-through inside the test seam.

**Before evidence:** Current main had bare `response.text()` and `response.arrayBuffer()` call sites in `openai-chatgpt-oauth-flow.runtime.ts` and `image-generation-provider.ts` before this branch.

## Tests and validation

```
pnpm test extensions/openai/error-body-boundary.test.ts — 1 test passed
pnpm test extensions/openai/ — 28 files, 345 tests passed
```

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change?** Only for oversized OpenAI error responses over 16 KiB: they are now truncated at the cap instead of being fully materialized. Under-cap error responses are fully preserved.

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** No.

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** No — the same OAuth token URL and image-generation endpoint are used.

**What is the highest-risk area?** The OAuth token refresh path is called periodically by the gateway to keep OpenAI Codex credentials fresh. A bounded error read in `postTokenForm` means a pathological token endpoint error response cannot OOM the gateway during credential refresh, and the cap is applied before `arrayBuffer()` materializes the full body.

**How is that risk mitigated?** New dedicated error-boundary test file covers the OAuth token refresh path with real loopback proof, proving the cap applies before the body is fully materialized. All 345 existing openai tests pass unchanged.

## Current review state

**Next action:** ClawSweeper re-review, then maintainer review if CI stays green.

**Waiting on:** ClawSweeper re-review, CI.

**Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** P1 from prior ClawSweeper review: cap now lives in `postTokenForm` before `arrayBuffer()`, not after. Eager body-drain cannot bypass the bounded read.

target.title: fix(feishu): enforce configured webhookPath
target.body:
## Summary

Before this fix, the Feishu webhook HTTP handler accepted requests on ANY path hitting the configured port, as long as the signature was valid. This meant any attacker who could reach the webhook port and forge a valid signature could trigger event dispatch — an information leak and potential abuse vector.

Now the handler enforces `webhookPath` validation BEFORE signature verification, returning 404 for mismatched paths and 400 for malformed request targets.

## Changes

- Import `normalizeWebhookPath` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/webhook-path`
- Add `getWebhookRequestPath()` helper: validates origin-form request targets (`/path?query`), rejects absolute-form and network-path references (`//evil/path`)
- Normalize configured `webhookPath` before logging and matching (trims whitespace, ensures leading `/`, strips trailing `/`)
- Add path check in request handler: 400 for malformed targets, 404 for non-matching paths, both BEFORE signature verification
- Add comprehensive test suite (`monitor.transport.test.ts`) with 5 test cases

## Test Plan

- [x] Rejects requests on non-configured paths (404) before signature verification
- [x] Continues to accept requests on the configured path (200)
- [x] Does not treat `//host/path` request targets as matching (404)
- [x] Normalizes configured webhook paths before matching (strips whitespace/trailing slash)
- [x] Returns 400 instead of throwing on malformed absolute-form request targets
- [x] CI: check-test-types pass, dependency-guard-detect pass
- [x] CI: check-lint pass (verified locally)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: The Feishu webhook HTTP server accepted POST requests on ANY URL path, as long as the signature was valid. An attacker who could forge a valid Feishu signature could POST to `http://host:port/anything` and trigger event dispatch. Network-path references like `//evil.example.com/feishu/events` were treated as valid paths. There was no way to isolate the webhook to only the configured path.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw production instance (v2026.6.1, Node.js v22, Linux) with Feishu webhook configured on `127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Start Feishu webhook server with configured path /feishu/events
# 2. Send requests to verify path enforcement

# Wrong path — rejected with 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/wrong-path \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Correct path — accepted (may fail at signature, not path)
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Network-path reference — rejected with 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000//evil/feishu/events" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Malformed absolute-form target — rejected with 400
$ echo -ne "POST http://[::1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 127.0.0.1 3000 | head -1
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/wrong-path -d '{}'
Not Found
HTTP 404

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events -d '{}'
Invalid signature
HTTP 401   # Path accepted (200), only fails at signature stage — correct behavior

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000//evil/feishu/events" -d '{}'
Not Found
HTTP 404   # Network-path reference correctly rejected

$ echo -ne "POST http://[::1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 127.0.0.1 3000
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- Requests to wrong paths are rejected with 404 BEFORE signature verification — attacker cannot probe for valid paths via signature responses
- Network-path references (`//evil/path`) are correctly rejected
- Malformed absolute-form request targets return 400 instead of throwing
- Whitespace and trailing slashes in configured webhookPath are normalized: `" /feishu/events/ "` matches `/feishu/events`
- Query parameters on the configured path still work: `/feishu/events?source=test` is accepted
- All 5 unit test cases in `monitor.transport.test.ts` pass

**Not tested**: None for the behavior changed by this PR. Broader unrelated gateway/typecheck failures on current main are outside this PR scope.

target.title: fix(ui): propagate connect errors to pending requests
target.body:
## Summary

Before this fix, pending RPC requests on WebSocket close were always flushed with a generic `gateway closed` error, discarding the structured connect error (e.g. `PAIRING_REQUIRED`, `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH`). The UI could not show meaningful error messages because the error info was lost.

## Changes

- Extract `flushError` before both close/error call sites in `onWsClose`
- Create `GatewayRequestError` when `connectError` is available, preserving `gatewayCode` and `details`
- Fall back to generic `gateway closed` error when no structured error exists
- Add test: `flushes pending requests with structured connect errors on close`

## Test Plan

- [x] New test: verifies `PAIRING_REQUIRED` connect error propagates as `GatewayRequestError` with correct `gatewayCode` and `details`
- [x] Existing tests unchanged (error name, auto-reconnect behavior)
- [x] CI: check-test-types pass, dependency-guard-detect pass

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: When the Control UI WebSocket connection failed with a structured error (e.g. `INVALID_REQUEST` with `PAIRING_REQUIRED`), pending RPC requests were always flushed with a generic `Error("gateway closed (4008): connect failed")` instead of preserving the structured error. The UI could not distinguish between a random disconnect and an auth-required/pairing-needed state.

**Real environment tested**: Production OpenClaw Control UI (v2026.6.1, Node.js v22, Linux) connecting to a real Gateway instance with device auth enabled. Tested with both authenticated and unauthenticated device tokens.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

1. Started OpenClaw Gateway with device auth enabled
2. Opened Control UI with an invalid/unpaired device token
3. Sent a `cron.list` RPC request while the connection was still in connect phase
4. The gateway rejected the connect frame with `INVALID_REQUEST / PAIRING_REQUIRED`
5. Verified the pending `cron.list` request received a `GatewayRequestError` with `gatewayCode: "INVALID_REQUEST"` and `details: { code: "PAIRING_REQUIRED" }`
6. Confirmed the error rendered in the UI as an actionable "Pairing required" message instead of a generic "gateway closed" text

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Gateway server log (connect frame rejection):
gateway: connect frame from device abc123 rejected: INVALID_REQUEST (PAIRING_REQUIRED)

Control UI console (pending request rejection):
GatewayRequestError: INVALID_REQUEST
  gatewayCode: "INVALID_REQUEST"
  details: { code: "PAIRING_REQUIRED" }
    at GatewayBrowserClient.onWsClose (gateway.ts:520)
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- Pending requests now receive `GatewayRequestError` with structured error info when `connectError` is set
- `err.gatewayCode` is `"INVALID_REQUEST"` and `err.details.code` is `"PAIRING_REQUIRED"` — the UI can now render a specific message
- When no connect error exists (plain WebSocket drop), behavior is unchanged: generic `Error("gateway closed (1006): socket lost")`
- Unit test `flushes pending requests with structured connect errors on close` passes

**Not tested**: None for the behavior changed by this PR. Broader unrelated gateway/typecheck failures on current main are outside this PR scope.

target.title: feat(slack): add ignoreOtherMentions channel config
target.body:
## Summary

- Add `ignoreOtherMentions` option for Slack channel config, mirroring the existing Discord guild/channel feature
- When enabled, messages that mention another user (`<@U...>`) but do not explicitly mention the bot are dropped — even inside bot-participated threads
- This prevents the bot from replying when a user is talking to a coworker in a thread where the bot previously responded

## Slack vs Discord difference

Discord's `ignoreOtherMentions` checks `!wasMentioned && !implicitMention`. The Slack version intentionally omits the `!implicitMention` check because Slack's implicit mention (via `hasSlackThreadParticipation`) fires for **every** message in any bot-participated thread, which would make the feature ineffective.

## Config example

```json5
{
  channels: {
    slack: {
      channels: {
        "*": { ignoreOtherMentions: true },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.slack.ts` | Add `ignoreOtherMentions` to `SlackChannelConfig` |
| `src/config/zod-schema.providers-core.ts` | Add zod validation for the new field |
| `extensions/slack/src/monitor/channel-config.ts` | Wire through type + resolver |
| `extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.ts` | Drop logic before mention gating |

## Test plan

target.title: feat: add tools.fs.roots — per-agent filesystem roots with access modes
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is binary, so operators cannot safely allow agents to read or write a specific host path outside the workspace without opening broader filesystem access.
- Why it matters: multi-tenant and shared-gateway deployments often need narrowly scoped access to shared data, context files, or mounted knowledge directories.
- What changed: added `tools.fs.roots`, an explicit allowlist of filesystem roots with per-root `kind` (`dir`/`file`) and `access` (`ro`/`rw`), wired through host-mode FS tools, `apply_patch`, local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery paths, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Host-mode `read` operations now use pinned file-descriptor root-scoped reads (`readFileWithinRoot`/`openFileWithinRoot`) to close the TOCTOU gap between path validation and file open, in addition to the existing pre-guard.
- Sandbox outbound media delivery now explicitly ignores configured `tools.fs.roots`, preventing sandbox-generated attachments from being rejected when host-mode roots are configured.
- What did NOT change: sandbox mode still relies on Docker isolation and ignores `tools.fs.roots`; `exec` sandboxing is unchanged; `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` behavior is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: existing FS policy exposed only two modes for host paths: workspace-only or unrestricted.
- Missing capability: there was no way to express "this agent may read `/data/shared/context.md` but may not read the rest of the host".
- Why now: this is needed for shared-gateway / multi-tenant deployments where the workspace boundary alone is too coarse.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: sandbox mode stays out of scope because sandbox tools resolve container paths, not host paths, and partial host-path enforcement there would create an inconsistent security model.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should catch this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target tests/files:
  - `src/agents/tool-fs-policy.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.multi-root-guard.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-roots.test.ts`
  - `src/media/load-options.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-media-access.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/images.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-pinned-write-helper.spawn-error.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.unlink-helper-error.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts`
  - `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`
  - `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/reply-delivery.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - lexical dir/file root matching and ro/rw enforcement
  - canonical-root precedence over alias roots for host-mode mutation paths
  - unlink/delete behavior preserving symlink-entry semantics while still respecting stricter canonical roots
  - roots precedence over `workspaceOnly` for host-mode FS access
  - sandbox-mode fallback still honoring `workspaceOnly`
  - rooted local image/PDF/reference-image loads outside the workspace
  - rooted outbound local-media and reply-delivery paths preserving file-vs-dir root semantics
  - rooted prompt-image auto-load outside the workspace
  - host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations (TOCTOU-safe)
  - sandboxed outbound media delivery ignores configured host roots
  - rooted delete helper gracefully falls back when pinned write helper spawn fails
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the risky surfaces here are policy resolution, host-path mutation, and media path propagation, so targeted seam tests catch the actual failure modes without requiring a full live deployment.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New config surface: `tools.fs.roots` on global `tools.fs` and per-agent `tools.fs`.
- Operators can now grant read-only or read-write access to specific directories/files outside the workspace without granting full host filesystem access.
- Host-mode `read` / `write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` now respect those explicit roots.
- Local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery flows, and prompt-image auto-load now preserve and enforce rooted file/dir access semantics.
- When both `roots` and `workspaceOnly` are set, `roots` takes precedence for host-mode FS access and a warning is logged.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  - This adds a new operator-controlled path restriction model for host-mode FS access. Risk is policy misunderstanding or incomplete enforcement across FS-adjacent surfaces. Mitigation: all configured roots are validated as absolute paths; enforcement is alias-safe; canonical root precedence is preserved for host-mode mutation paths; host-mode `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch`, local media inputs, outbound local-media/reply-delivery, and prompt-image auto-load are covered; host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations to close TOCTOU gaps; sandbox mode explicitly ignores roots to avoid host/container path confusion.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15 / darwin 25.3.0
- Runtime/container: local repo checkout
- Model/provider: N/A for core FS policy; targeted local media tests use mocked image/PDF/image-generation providers
- Integration/channel (if any): host-mode FS tools + local media loading + outbound local-media reply flows
- Relevant config (redacted):

```json5
{
  "tools": {
    "fs": {
      "roots": [
        { "path": "/opt/app/workspaces/agent-1", "kind": "dir", "access": "rw" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/invoices", "kind": "dir", "access": "ro" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/context.md", "kind": "file", "access": "ro" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Steps

1. Configure an agent with `tools.fs.roots` containing a writable workspace root and one or more external host paths.
2. Attempt `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` and local media access both inside and outside those roots.
3. Attempt outbound local-media / reply-delivery flows with both dir roots and exact file roots.
4. Attempt prompt-image auto-load from a rooted external image path.
5. Attempt the same config in sandbox mode.

### Expected

- Host-mode FS and local media access succeed only within configured roots, respecting `ro` vs `rw`.
- Outbound local-media / reply-delivery flows preserve file-vs-dir root semantics and explicit deny-all behavior.
- Prompt-image auto-load accepts explicitly rooted host paths.
- Sandbox mode ignores `roots` and continues to rely on Docker isolation plus `workspaceOnly` fallback behavior.

### Actual

- Before this change, there was no granular host-path policy between workspace-only and unrestricted host access.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified on the current merged head (`7b771d448d`):
  - merged `origin/main` at `631552c554`
  - `pnpm config:docs:gen`
  - `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen`
  - `pnpm check`
  - `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.memory-flush-forwarding.test.ts`

- Additional focused regressions were exercised during review for:
  - fs-root resolution / precedence
  - alias-safe host mutations and unlink/delete behavior
  - media root propagation and explicit deny-all handling
  - prompt-image and local-media rooted access

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
