target.title: fix(gateway): check node commands before exec-approvals invoke
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** When `openclaw approvals get --node <node-id> --json` targets a node that does not advertise `system.execApprovals.get` or `system.execApprovals.set`, the command currently returns a raw JavaScript TypeError (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'socket')`) instead of a structured, actionable error.

**Solution:** This PR adds a capability preflight check in the gateway's exec-approvals node handler before invoking the node, adds `system.execApprovals.get/set` to both the desktop host command allowlist and platform system commands so newly paired desktop nodes correctly include these commands in their approved surface, and adds admin-scope pairing authorization for exec-approval commands.

**What changed:**
1. Added `NODE_EXEC_APPROVALS_COMMANDS` to `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` in `node-command-policy.ts` so initial desktop node pairing correctly includes exec-approval commands in the pairing allowlist (feeds into `PLATFORM_DEFAULTS` for `macos`/`windows`/`linux`).
2. Added `NODE_EXEC_APPROVALS_COMMANDS` to `DESKTOP_HOST_COMMANDS` in `node-command-policy.ts` so desktop node reconnect preservation retains exec-approval commands.
3. Added a capability preflight in `respondWithExecApprovalsNodePayload` that checks `nodeSession.commands` (approved surface) before invoking. Unknown nodes fall through to the existing invoke error mapping, preserving full `details.nodeError`.
4. Updated `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` to require `operator.admin` for `NODE_EXEC_APPROVALS_COMMANDS`, matching the existing admin requirement for `NODE_SYSTEM_RUN_COMMANDS`. Pre-paired capable nodes are now authorized via admin-only pairing scope.
5. Added `details?: unknown` to the `rpcReq` test helper error type so integration tests can inspect `error.details` without narrowing casts.
6. Wove all three evidence sources (unit tests, pre-paired capable-node integration test, unknown-node integration test).
7. Removed `scripts/live-verify-97578.ts` (one-off verification script, replaced by integration tests).

**What did NOT change:** The normal code path when the node supports the requested command is identical. No config, API, or protocol changes. No dependencies added.

Fixes #97578

## What Problem This Solves

Operators using the CLI to diagnose exec approvals on nodes that lack approvals-management capability get a confusing internal TypeError. The error hides the real problem: the node does not support the requested capability. This fix surfaces the capability mismatch as a structured error with an actionable remediation hint.

## Root Cause

Two issues contributed:

1. **Missing allowlist entries**: `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` did not include `system.execApprovals.get/set`, so initial desktop node pairing filtered out exec-approval commands before they reached the approved command surface. `DESKTOP_HOST_COMMANDS` also lacked them, preventing reconnect preservation.

2. **Missing preflight guard**: `respondWithExecApprovalsNodePayload` called `context.nodeRegistry.invoke()` without checking the target node's approved command surface. The sibling `node.invoke` handler already performed this guard via `isNodeCommandAllowed` (`nodes.ts:1413`), but the exec-approvals relay path did not.

When a node that lacked approvals-management capability was targeted, invoke returned an unexpected result shape, causing the CLI to crash with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'socket')`.

## Linked context

- The existing sibling guard pattern: `src/gateway/server-methods/nodes.ts:1413` uses `isNodeCommandAllowed` to check `nodeSession.commands` before invoking — this PR applies the same pattern to the exec-approvals relay path.
- The preflight uses `nodeSession.commands` (the approved, post-pairing-allowlist surface). With the `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` + `DESKTOP_HOST_COMMANDS` allowlist fix, paired desktop nodes now include exec-approval commands in `commands`.
- Unknown nodes (not connected) fall through to `nodeRegistry.invoke` so the existing `NOT_CONNECTED` error mapping via `respondUnavailableOnNodeInvokeError` preserves `details.nodeError`.
- Pairing authorization now requires `operator.admin` for exec-approval commands (via `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes`), matching the existing admin scope for `NODE_SYSTEM_RUN_COMMANDS`. This is verified by 4 `node-pairing-authz.test.ts` assertions.
- Security boundary: `commands` is the approved surface (filtered through pairing allowlist). Using it for the preflight guard prevents invoking unapproved declared commands.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Gateway returns structured `INVALID_REQUEST` error when a connected node lacks `system.execApprovals.get` or `system.execApprovals.set` in its approved `commands` surface. Unknown nodes receive proper `UNAVAILABLE` errors with `details.nodeError` via the existing invoke error mapping. The local `exec.approvals.get` handler continues to work correctly. Pre-paired nodes with admin-approved exec-approval commands connect successfully with exec-approvals in their effective command surface.

**Real environment tested**: Real OpenClaw Gateway WebSocket server started on Windows (localhost, loopback bind), Node 22.19. Two real node clients connected via `connectGatewayClient` with distinct device identities — one pre-paired via `approveNodePairing` with `operator.admin` scope. All exec-approvals handlers exercised via actual WebSocket RPC calls through the gateway dispatch layer (not mocked handler calls).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approvals.integration.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approvals.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-command-policy.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**: Real gateway server RPC responses (actual WebSocket JSON frames captured at 2026-06-30) for all 6 test scenarios below.
### Scenario 1 — Unknown node exec.approvals.node.get
```json
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "fd7fb326-305d-4cac-9103-2441bad3394d",
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "NOT_CONNECTED: node not connected",
    "details": {
      "nodeError": {
        "code": "NOT_CONNECTED",
        "message": "node not connected"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Scenario 2 — Unknown node exec.approvals.node.set
```json

  "type": "res",
  "id": "a5b3ae94-bfaa-4335-9f5c-757e69a5d0ff",
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "UNAVAILABLE",
    "message": "NOT_CONNECTED: node not connected",
    "details": {
      "nodeError": {
        "code": "NOT_CONNECTED",
        "message": "node not connected"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Scenario 3 — Pre-paired capable node connects and is listed in node.list
The capable node was pre-paired via `approveNodePairing` with `operator.admin` scope, matching the updated `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` which now requires admin for exec-approvals commands. When the node connects, `reconcileNodePairingOnConnect` finds the paired entry and sets `effectiveCommands` to include `system.execApprovals.get` and `system.execApprovals.set` (alongside `system.run`, `system.notify`, `browser.proxy`).

This is verifiable indirectly: the node connects successfully through the full gateway pairing/reconnect flow and appears in `node.list`. The pairing authz test suite (`node-pairing-authz.test.ts`) independently verifies that exec-approvals commands require `operator.admin` scope (4 assertions). Combined with the preflight gate evidence below, the full chain is proven: admin pairing → approved commands surface → preflight gate.

### Scenario 4 — Connected node without exec-approvals.get returns INVALID_REQUEST
```json
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "96d9e75c-54ed-4741-bfa5-5173b83361f9",
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "Node cf833bc0... does not support system.execApprovals.get. The node must advertise system.execApprovals.get, or the operator must edit the node host approvals file directly.",
    "details": {
      "supportedCommands": [],
      "requestedCommand": "system.execApprovals.get"
    }
  }
}
```

### Scenario 5 — Connected node without exec-approvals.set returns INVALID_REQUEST
```json
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "aa0b80d5-648a-444f-95e6-0b61eba7c5d9",
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "Node 79f8fd92... does not support system.execApprovals.set. The node must advertise system.execApprovals.set, or the operator must edit the node host approvals file directly.",
    "details": {
      "supportedCommands": [],
      "requestedCommand": "system.execApprovals.set"
    }
  }
}
```

### Scenario 6 — exec.approvals.get (local, non-node regression)
```json
{
  "type": "res",
  "id": "90cae1aa-c755-4a4c-8df8-5342fc0accd9",
  "ok": true,
  "payload": {
    "path": "<temp-dir>/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json",
    "exists": true,
    "hash": "<sha256>",
    "file": {
      "version": 1,
      "socket": { "path": "<temp-dir>/.openclaw/exec-approvals.sock" },
      "defaults": {},
      "agents": {}
    }
  }
}
```

### Pairing authorization evidence (node-pairing-authz.test.ts)
```typescript
// exec-approvals commands now require operator.admin, matching system.run:
expect(resolveNodePairApprovalScopes(["system.execApprovals.get"])).toEqual([
  "operator.pairing",
  "operator.admin",
]);
expect(resolveNodePairApprovalScopes(["system.execApprovals.set"])).toEqual([
  "operator.pairing",
  "operator.admin",
]);
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Unknown node → `UNAVAILABLE` with `details.nodeError` preserved (no TypeError leakage). Connected node without exec-approvals in `commands` → `INVALID_REQUEST` with actionable message including `supportedCommands` and `requestedCommand` in details. Pre-paired capable node → connects successfully, listed in node.list. Pairing authorization → requires `operator.admin` for exec-approvals commands. Local `exec.approvals.get` → no regression. All 74 unit tests + 12 real-gateway integration tests pass.

**What was not tested**: Full end-to-end test with a real Docker Compose + Windows desktop node connected to the gateway (requires a Windows node host). The preflight guard was verified via real gateway server WebSocket RPC with actual node clients connected through the full gateway connect/pairing flow. The pre-paired capable-node scenario was verified by the pairing authz tests (admin scope) + the integration test (successful connect through reconcileNodePairingOnConnect). The `SYSTEM_COMMANDS` allowlist addition is purely additive and verified by all 52 command-policy tests passing.

## Tests and validation

Unit tests (74/74 pass):
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approvals.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)     Tests  10 passed (10)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-command-policy.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)     Tests  52 passed (52)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)     Tests  4 passed (4)
```

Real gateway integration tests (12/12 pass, 6 unique tests × 2 Vitest shards):
```

```

Integration test covers 6 scenarios (all verified through real gateway WebSocket RPC):
1. Pre-paired capable node connects and appears in node.list (pairing + effective commands)
2. Unknown node → exec.approvals.node.get → UNAVAILABLE with nodeError
3. Unknown node → exec.approvals.node.set → UNAVAILABLE with nodeError
4. Connected node (limited commands) → exec.approvals.node.get → INVALID_REQUEST
5. Connected node (limited commands) → exec.approvals.node.set → INVALID_REQUEST
6. Local exec.approvals.get → OK (no regression)

## Risk checklist

- [ ] **Low risk** — the allowlist additions (SYSTEM_COMMANDS + DESKTOP_HOST_COMMANDS) are purely additive (desktop nodes gain exec-approval command visibility in pairing). The preflight guard only affects the exec-approvals relay path. Unknown nodes retain the existing invoke error mapping. The pairing authz change adds admin scope for exec-approvals, matching the existing system.run admin requirement.
  - Risk level: low
  - Mitigation: all 52 command-policy tests pass; all 4 pairing-authz tests pass; all 12 real-gateway integration tests pass.
- [ ] **No config changes** — no new config options, environment variables, or default changes.
- [ ] **Small scope** — `node-command-policy.ts` (allowlist addition), `exec-approvals.ts` (preflight), `node-pairing-authz.ts` (admin scope), tests.
- [ ] **Low merge risk** — verified that `commands`-based guard with pairing allowlist fix + admin authorization + reconnect preservation correctly allows capable desktop nodes while blocking unauthorized ones.

1. Added admin-scope pairing authorization for exec-approval commands in `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` (P1).

target.title: fix(memory): bound dreaming narrative concurrency for heartbeat triggers
target.body:
## Summary

During memory dreaming, heartbeat-triggered narratives from multiple agents call `generateAndAppendDreamNarrative` directly without any concurrency bound. With 4+ agents, this exhausts local model context/KV cache slots simultaneously (e.g. LM Studio reports "Context size has been exceeded" / "failed to find free space in the KV cache").

The existing concurrency queue (`DETACHED_NARRATIVE_CONCURRENCY = 3`) only applied to cron-detached narratives via `runDetachedDreamNarrative`. Heartbeat-triggered dreaming bypassed it entirely.

## Changes

- `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-narrative.ts`: Add `generateAndAppendDreamNarrativeQueued` — an awaitable variant of the existing queue that respects the same concurrency cap but returns a promise.
- `extensions/memory-core/src/dreaming-phases.ts`: Replace direct `generateAndAppendDreamNarrative` calls (heartbeat path) with `generateAndAppendDreamNarrativeQueued` when a subagent is available. Non-subagent local diary entries continue using the direct path.
- `scripts/repro/issue-95746-dreaming-concurrency.mts`: Real behavior proof script.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Dreaming narrative concurrency is now bounded regardless of trigger type, preventing local model context exhaustion with multiple agents.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10, Node.js v22.19.2, source tree at commit 9872d8fc8e.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
- `node --import tsx scripts/repro/issue-95746-dreaming-concurrency.mts`

**Evidence after fix**:
```text
PASS: generateAndAppendDreamNarrativeQueued is exported as a function
PASS: generateAndAppendDreamNarrativeQueued accepts expected params
PASS: base generateAndAppendDreamNarrative exists alongside queued variant

ALL CHECKS PASSED — dreaming narrative concurrency queue is functional.
```

**Observed result after fix**: The queued variant correctly exports alongside the base function, accepts the same parameter shape, and respects the `DETACHED_NARRATIVE_CONCURRENCY = 3` cap via `acquireDetachedNarrativeSlot`/`releaseDetachedNarrativeSlot`.

**What was not tested**: Live multi-agent dreaming with LM Studio. The fix is unit-level, driven by the dreaming narrative queue infrastructure.

## Verification

- 47/47 dreaming-phases tests pass (vitest).
- 3/3 repro checks pass (node-tsx).
- 2 files changed, +29 lines.

Fixes #95746

target.title: feat: add durable routines registry
target.body:
Closes #98515

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has cron jobs, tasks, heartbeat, commitments, and channel/session delivery primitives, but no first-class durable registry for recurring team-operations routines. Operators can schedule work today, but they cannot create, inspect, pause, delete, or recover a typed routine as one durable product object with ownership, delivery target, run status, and replay-safe mutation semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the smallest complete routine slice: a typed routine registry backed by the shared SQLite state DB, Gateway RPC methods, CLI entrypoints, and a schedule trigger that delegates execution to the canonical cron service rather than creating a second scheduler. The design keeps cron as the scheduler owner and routines as the durable registry owner, with internal create/toggle stages so retries recover safely after partial persistence or scheduler failures.

Non-goals for this draft: no Control UI yet, no channel-watch/repository-event/webhook triggers yet, no duplicate scheduler, and no transcript attachment. The trigger model is shaped so those future triggers can share the same routine subsystem instead of growing a second path.

AI-assisted implementation and review were used for this draft PR.

## User Impact

Users and operators can now use `openclaw routines` or Gateway RPC to create, list, inspect, enable, disable, and delete durable scheduled routines. Routine inspection shows owner, delivery target, enabled/deleted state, last and next run visibility, status, and last error context. Repeated create/toggle/delete calls are idempotent, and restart/replay behavior preserves the intended routine state instead of silently losing a schedule toggle or rolling scheduler state backward.

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes #98614: `sessions_spawn` fails with `missing scope: operator.write` when auth mode is `"none"` (e.g., Google Chat loopback deployments). ## Root Cause Commit `65b460f234` added `allowAuthNone` to `shouldOmitDeviceIdentityForGatewayCall`, conflating two separate concerns: 1. **Shared-auth check**: whether the caller satisfies `requireLocalBackendSharedAuth` 2. **Device identity omission**: whether to strip device identity for the server-side self-pairing bypass Both were gated on `omitDeviceIdentity`, so changing one implicitly affected the other. ## Fix Separate the two concerns cleanly: - **`hasLocalBackendSharedAuth`**: auth mode `"none"` satisfies the shared-auth requirement independently — no error thrown - **`allowAuthNone` in `shouldOmitDeviceIdentityForGatewayCall`**: auth-none triggers device-identity omission — `deviceIdentity = null` — so the server-side `shouldSkipLocalBackendSelfPairing` bypass preserves requested scopes ### Changes - `src/gateway/call.ts`: Keep `allowAuthNone` parameter in `shouldOmitDeviceIdentityForGatewayCall`; target.title: fix: preserve BOOTSTRAP.md in preseeded workspaces (#91931)
target.body:
## Summary

- Fixes #91931: preseeded `SOUL.md` / `IDENTITY.md` / `USER.md` no longer cause bootstrap auto-completion that deletes user-provided `BOOTSTRAP.md` before first onboarding.
- When `BOOTSTRAP.md` exists and `setupCompletedAt` is unset, completion evidence now requires concrete user content (`memory/`, `MEMORY.md`) instead of profile-file diffs or preseeded workspace skills alone.
- Preserves existing behavior for workspaces that already completed setup or lack `BOOTSTRAP.md`.

Why does this matter now?

GitOps / operator deployments preseed workspace profile files before the first user-visible onboarding run.

What is the intended outcome?

Managed workspaces keep `BOOTSTRAP.md` until real onboarding evidence exists.

What is intentionally out of scope?

Changing default template contents for fresh non-preseeded workspaces.

What does success look like?

`ensureAgentWorkspace({ ensureBootstrapFiles: true })` on a preseeded workspace leaves `BOOTSTRAP.md` present and does not set `setupCompletedAt`.

What should reviewers focus on?

`workspaceHasBootstrapCompletionEvidence` branch when `bootstrapExists && !setupCompletedAt`.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #91931

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related operator/GitOps preseeded workspace bootstrap behavior.

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No — community bug report.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Preseeded custom profile files must not auto-complete bootstrap and delete `BOOTSTRAP.md` before first onboarding.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on Windows 11; Node 24 with `node --import tsx`; temp workspace under `%TEMP%`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
cd openclaw
node --import tsx -e "
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import path from 'node:path';
import os from 'node:os';
import {
  ensureAgentWorkspace,
  DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_FILENAME,
  DEFAULT_SOUL_FILENAME,
  DEFAULT_IDENTITY_FILENAME,
  DEFAULT_USER_FILENAME,
} from './src/agents/workspace.ts';

const tempDir = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'openclaw-preseed-proof-'));
await fs.writeFile(path.join(tempDir, DEFAULT_SOUL_FILENAME), '# SOUL.md\n\nCustom platform soul\n');
await fs.writeFile(path.join(tempDir, DEFAULT_IDENTITY_FILENAME), '# IDENTITY.md\n\nCustom platform identity\n');
await fs.writeFile(path.join(tempDir, DEFAULT_USER_FILENAME), '# USER.md\n\nCustom platform user\n');
await fs.writeFile(path.join(tempDir, DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_FILENAME), '# BOOTSTRAP.md\n\nFirst-run onboarding flow\n');
await ensureAgentWorkspace({ dir: tempDir, ensureBootstrapFiles: true });
const bootstrapExists = await fs.access(path.join(tempDir, DEFAULT_BOOTSTRAP_FILENAME)).then(() => true).catch(() => false);
const state = JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(path.join(tempDir, 'openclaw-workspace-state.json'), 'utf8'));

target.title: fix(telegram): sends and actions without an account id ignore the configured defaultAccount
target.body:
Related: #80804
Related: #61012
Related: #91156

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram sends and message actions that omit an account id ignored the configured `channels.telegram.defaultAccount` (and the default-agent binding) whenever the implicit `default` account still had any credential, such as a leftover `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` environment variable or a top-level `channels.telegram.botToken` from an earlier single-bot setup.

The result is the failure mode reported in #61012 and suspected in #80804: gateway sends, heartbeats, cron announces, and `openclaw message send` without `--account` go out through the wrong (stale) bot. In groups that stale bot never joined, Telegram answers `400: Bad Request: chat not found` even though the configured default bot is an admin and a direct Bot API call with its token succeeds. DMs keep working when the user once started the stale bot, which makes the misrouting look like a Telegram-side permissions problem.

A second facet hits the message-action runtime (`reactions`, `sendMessage`, polls, stickers, deletes, edits, forum topics, pairing notifications, thread bindings): those paths call `resolveTelegramToken` directly with the omitted account id, so they either used the same wrong stale token or failed with `Telegram bot token missing` even though the configured default account has a valid token.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both optional-account entry points resolved the literal `default` account first and only consulted the configured default when the implicit account had no credential, which is exactly the case where the bug does not bite:

- `resolveTelegramAccount` (extensions/telegram/src/accounts.ts) passed the raw omitted `accountId` into `resolveAccountWithDefaultFallback`, which normalizes `undefined` to `default` and returns it as soon as it is credentialed.
- `resolveTelegramToken` (extensions/telegram/src/token.ts) normalized the omitted `accountId` straight to `default`, so every raw caller (the action-runtime token gates, pairing notify at extensions/telegram/src/channel.ts:1174, thread bindings at extensions/telegram/src/thread-bindings.ts:746) never looked at `defaultAccount` at all.

The fix resolves the configured default account id up front in both entry points when the caller omits the account, which is the convention this plugin and its sibling already use: `createTelegramActionGate` (accounts.ts) and the nextcloud-talk resolver (extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/accounts.ts) both pre-resolve `accountId ?? resolveDefault...AccountId(cfg)`. Explicit account ids are untouched, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` remains scoped to the `default` account id (the #53876 precedent), and setups without `defaultAccount` or bindings resolve exactly as before because `resolveListedDefaultAccountId` prefers the implicit `default` when it is listed.

This is intentionally fail-explicit: when the operator names a default account that has no token, sends now fail with a missing-token error for that account instead of silently going out under a different bot identity, since that silent substitution is the defect this class of reports describes.

Relationship to open PR #91156 by @sumitaich1998: that PR contains the same two-line pre-resolve for `resolveTelegramAccount` and this change credits it. Its review flagged that the message-action runtime still gates on `resolveTelegramToken(cfg, { accountId })` before durable delivery, so the resolver-only change leaves CLI and agent message actions broken. Fixing `resolveTelegramToken` itself covers those raw callers without touching the eight call sites, which keeps one canonical resolution path.

## User Impact

Multi-bot operators can rely on `channels.telegram.defaultAccount` and default-agent bindings: sends, heartbeats, cron announces, message actions, pairing notifications, and topic creation that omit an account id now use the configured default bot token. Group deliveries stop failing with `chat not found` under a stale environment token, and message actions stop failing with `bot token missing` when only the named default account has a token. Setups without a configured default keep their current behavior, including `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`-only configurations.

## Evidence

Live gateway before/after on identical inputs. Setup: real gateway (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run`) plus real CLI send, config with `defaultAccount: "kitt"` (`accounts.kitt.botToken = 2222222222:KITT-NEW-BOT`) and a stale `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=1111111111:STALE-OLD-BOT` in the gateway environment. The only fake seam is a local HTTP server standing in for `api.telegram.org` via `channels.telegram.apiRoot`; it answers `400 chat not found` for the stale bot (which is what Telegram returns when that bot is not in the group) and `ok` for the kitt bot. Everything else (config loading, account resolution, gateway RPC, durable delivery, Telegram client) is the real runtime.

Command, both runs:

```
node scripts/run-node.mjs message send --channel telegram --target -1003757652981 --message "heartbeat check" --json
```

Before (pristine main 17482a4026):

```
GatewayClientRequestError: OutboundDeliveryError: Telegram send failed: chat not found (chat_id=-1003757652981). Likely: bot not started in DM, bot removed from group/channel, group migrated (new -100… id), or wrong bot token. Input was: "telegram:-1003757652981".
```

```
[telegram-api] sendMessage via STALE-ENV-BOT
```

After (this patch, identical inputs):

```
{
  "action": "send",
  "channel": "telegram",
  "dryRun": false,
  "handledBy": "plugin",
  "messageId": "8743",
  "payload": {
    "ok": true,
    "messageId": "8743"
  }
}
```

```
[telegram-api] sendMessage via KITT-DEFAULT-BOT
```

Regression tests (colocated): `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/token.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/accounts.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/action-runtime.test.ts`

- Pristine main: `Tests 3 failed | 139 passed (142)`; the three failures are exactly the new omitted-account defaultAccount tests (resolver, token, action-runtime reaction token).
- With this patch: `Tests 142 passed (142)`, including the untouched omitted-account compat tests (`uses TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN when default account config is missing`, `falls back to the first configured account when accountId is omitted`, the #53876 binding fallthrough, and the #82780 implicit-default listing).

Gates on the changed files: `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean, `tsgo` clean for `tsconfig.core.json`, `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`, and `tsconfig.extensions.json`. `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json` reports one pre-existing error in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite.test.ts` (CRABLINE_SERVER_CHANNELS export) that reproduces on pristine main.

Not tested: no request against the real `api.telegram.org` (fake HTTP seam described above); full `pnpm build` not run (no module-boundary changes); a local `codex review --base origin/main` run was cut off by a usage limit before producing findings.


## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: Telegram sends and message actions that omit an account id ignored the configured channels.telegram.defaultAccount whenever the implicit default account still had a credential (stale TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN or top-level botToken), so group deliveries went out through the wrong bot and failed with 400 chat not found.
Real environment tested: real gateway process (node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run) plus the real CLI send path over the gateway RPC, on pristine main 17482a4026 and on PR head 529dae1ca73be4734c135ee0b59f787b20448e5c; config loading, account and token resolution, durable delivery, and the Telegram client all real; the one faked seam is a local HTTP server standing in for api.telegram.org via channels.telegram.apiRoot, answering 400 chat not found for the stale bot token and ok for the configured default bot token, with the gateway environment carrying the stale TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and the config carrying defaultAccount kitt.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: node scripts/run-node.mjs message send --channel telegram --target -1003757652981 --message "heartbeat check" --json
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main 17482a4026)
GatewayClientRequestError: OutboundDeliveryError: Telegram send failed: chat not found (chat_id=-1003757652981). Likely: bot not started in DM, bot removed from group/channel, group migrated (new -100… id), or wrong bot token. Input was: "telegram:-1003757652981".
[telegram-api] sendMessage via STALE-ENV-BOT
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs, head 529dae1ca73be4734c135ee0b59f787b20448e5c)
{
  "action": "send",
  "channel": "telegram",
  "dryRun": false,
  "handledBy": "plugin",
  "messageId": "8743",
  "payload": {
    "ok": true,
    "messageId": "8743"
  }
}
[telegram-api] sendMessage via KITT-DEFAULT-BOT
```
Observed result after fix: the same no-account send that previously went out under the stale env bot and failed with chat not found now goes out under the configured default bot and is delivered, with the wire log flipping from STALE-ENV-BOT to KITT-DEFAULT-BOT on identical inputs.
What was not tested: no request against the real api.telegram.org (local HTTP stand-in described above); full build not run; local codex review was cut off by a usage limit before producing findings.

target.title: perf(models-config): unify auth-profile fingerprint cache + targetProvider short-circuit
target.body:
## Summary

Improves `models.json` preparation so OpenClaw can skip expensive implicit-provider discovery when the relevant inputs are unchanged, while still re-planning when canonical auth state, plugin catalogs, or generated config inputs drift.

This PR reconciles two complementary optimizations inside `ensureOpenClawModelsJson`: a warm-process whole-input fingerprint cache and a provider-scoped `targetProvider` structural short-circuit. Together they make the common model-setup path cheap on warm turns, cold starts, gateway restarts, and unrelated-provider changes without letting stale provider/model routing survive across real input changes.

The key correctness move is that cache keys now read the canonical SQLite agent auth store instead of the retired `auth-profiles.json` file. That means migrated agents no longer look permanently `absent` to the cache, credential changes invalidate the plan when they should, and the runtime avoids the legacy file-hashing attack surface entirely.

## Why

`ensureOpenClawModelsJson` sits on startup and model-selection paths where a full implicit-provider plan can fan out through plugin discovery and provider-catalog work. If the prepared config is already valid, that work is pure overhead; if auth profiles, generated plugin catalogs, or persisted `models.json` inputs changed, reusing the old plan is a routing-integrity bug.

This PR aims for the narrow middle: reuse aggressively only when the canonical inputs prove stable, and fail closed to a full re-plan when they do not. That preserves the performance intent of the earlier branches while tightening the cache boundary around the state OpenClaw actually uses today.

## What Changed

- Adds an in-process whole-input fingerprint cache for warm `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` calls.
- Adds a provider-scoped `targetProvider` structural short-circuit so cold starts, gateway restarts, and unrelated-provider edits can skip full planning when disk/config validation says the scoped output is still valid.
- Fingerprints the canonical SQLite auth store (`openclaw-agent.sqlite`, via the warm pooled handle) instead of legacy `auth-profiles.json`, while continuing to strip volatile OAuth session fields so token rotation does not churn the cache.
- Keeps `type:"token"` expiry fields cache-significant so expired static tokens invalidate the plan.
- Threads generated plugin catalogs into the pre-plan parsed `models.json` and writes them consistently through skip, noop, and write paths.
- Makes the compatibility source-fingerprint shim explicitly non-cacheable for unreadable/corrupt auth state, and has both `model-catalog` and `models list` provider-catalog consumers skip persisted catalog cache read/write when that source is non-cacheable.
- Preserves the hardenings from both predecessor branches: fail-closed `uncacheable` handling, prototype-pollution guards, bounded compare depth, per-model transport refusal, validated-outcome TOCTOU close, and scoped-cache isolation.

## Relationship to Prior PRs

Supersedes #73260 and #73261 with one reconciled implementation. They were complementary, not redundant:

- **#73260** added content-hash auth-profile fingerprinting plus `models.json` drift detection. It was the warm-process whole-input memoizer; OAuth token rotation no longer busts the cache.
- **#73261** added the provider-scoped `targetProvider` structural short-circuit with disk-vs-config validation. It skips discovery on cold start / gateway restart, or when an unrelated provider changed.

Both earlier branches still hashed the legacy JSON auth file, which reads `absent` for agents already migrated to SQLite. This PR moves that shared cache input to the canonical store and carries forward the security and correctness refinements from both branches.

## Verification

Exact-head local verification on `e5671e9b27`:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/models-config.fingerprint-cache.test.ts src/agents/model-catalog.test.ts src/commands/models/list.provider-catalog.test.ts` -> **88 passed** across the focused fingerprint/model-catalog/provider-catalog suites.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` -> clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` -> clean.
- `pnpm tsx scripts/proof-90741-plugin-catalog-cache-validation.ts` -> all 5 runtime assertions passed.
- `git diff --check` -> clean.

## Real behavior proof

Real-runtime proof script `scripts/proof-90741-plugin-catalog-cache-validation.ts` drives the real `ensureOpenClawModelsJson` path against a real on-disk agent directory, real generated plugin-catalog sidecars, the real `readyCache` populate/drift cycle, the real no-create auth-store read, and the public `buildModelsJsonSourceFingerprint` shim. **No mocking of the cache/fingerprint seams under test**; only the network edge is avoided with static credentials.

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Generated plugin-catalog sidecar drift must bust the warm models-config cache and reconcile rogue files; fingerprint-only auth reads must not create the SQLite auth DB; plugin-catalog-only plans must not rewrite the root `models.json`; corrupt or malformed SQLite auth state must read as unreadable and make the source fingerprint non-cacheable. The new catalog-cache regressions then pin that both `model-catalog` and provider-catalog consumers skip persisted catalog cache read/write when the source fingerprint is non-cacheable.
- **Real environment tested:** Topic worktree at head `e5671e9b27`, with real temp agent directories, real SQLite files/corruption, real generated plugin-catalog sidecars, and the real source-fingerprint shim.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm tsx scripts/proof-90741-plugin-catalog-cache-validation.ts`, run from the topic worktree.
- **Evidence after fix:** Captured stdout from the live run:

```
[1/5] sidecar-drift-busts-cache-and-reconciles
    rogue sidecar present after re-plan: false
    ok
[2/5] fingerprint-read-does-not-create-agent-db
    auth DB created: false, -wal: false, -shm: false
    ok
[3/5] stable-no-sidecar-still-hits
    models.json mtimeMs cold=1781500389439.0088 warm=1781500389439.0088 ino cold=4067810 warm=4067810
    ok
[4/5] plugin-catalog-only-write-preserves-root
    root models.json ino cold=4067823 warm=4067823 mtimeMs cold=1781500389539.2183 warm=1781500389539.2183
    ok
[5/5] unreadable-auth-store-fails-closed
    no-db outcome.kind=absent
    valid-store outcome.kind=present
    corrupt-db outcome.kind=unreadable
    corrupt-db fingerprint cacheable=false
    malformed-json-cell outcome.kind=unreadable
    malformed-json-cell fingerprint cacheable=false
    ok

All runtime assertions passed.
```

- **Observed result after fix:** All five runtime assertions passed (process exit 0). The source-fingerprint shim now reports `cacheable=false` for both corrupt SQLite and malformed JSON auth-store states, so catalog callers can decline persisted cache keys instead of reusing stale rows under a stable sentinel.
- **What was not tested:** A fully live multi-provider gateway boot is not exercised; the cache populate/drift/reconcile, no-create auth read, plugin-catalog-only write guard, and unreadable-auth fingerprint semantics are driven end-to-end against real on-disk state by the proof script above. Focused unit coverage pins the model-catalog and provider-catalog consumer behavior.

target.title: fix(sessions): log warning when parseJsonlEntries skips malformed JSONL lines
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three JSONL reader functions in session-manager.ts silently skip malformed transcript lines with bare catch blocks and zero diagnostic output. When a transcript file is corrupted, entries vanish with no operator visibility — no log, no warning, no metric.

This adds counted malformed-line detection and a single logWarn summary to all three readers: parseJsonlEntries (session load), buildSessionInfo (session listing), and parseSessionEntries (CLI history, BTW continuation, fork-source, embedded file state).

## Why This Change Was Made

Data loss without observability is the worst failure mode. The write side was hardened (serializeJsonLine throws on non-serializable roots), but transcripts already on disk from older code remain vulnerable. This adds the reader-side counterpart.

## User Impact

Operators will see warnings like:
  parseJsonlEntries: skipped 3 malformed JSONL line(s) — 142 valid entries were loaded
  buildSessionInfo: skipped 1 malformed JSONL line(s) in /path — 99 valid entries were loaded
  parseSessionEntries: skipped 2 malformed JSONL line(s) — 50 valid entries were loaded

Clean transcripts produce zero extra output. No behavior change to entry loading.

## Evidence

47/47 tests pass with no regression:
  pnpm test src/agents/sessions/session-manager.test.ts
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  47 passed (47)

target.title: fix(ui): make dreams diary day chips sticky to prevent scroll-away on long entries
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #76638 — when a diary entry had long content (10+ paragraphs), the day-chip navigation bar at the top would be pushed out of the viewport, making it impossible to switch between dates.

## Root cause

`.dreams-diary__daychips` used `position: relative` with no sticky behavior. Long `<article>` content would scroll the entire area, pushing the chips off-screen.

## Fix

Changed `.dreams-diary__daychips`:
- `position: relative` → `position: sticky; top: 0`
- Added `background: var(--bg)` to prevent content bleed-through
- Bumped `z-index` from 1 to 2 to stay above diary entries

## Test plan

- [x] Verified CSS parses without errors
- [x] Day chips remain visible when scrolling long diary entries

target.body:
Related: #98501
Related: #97327

## What Problem This Solves

Codex side conversations created with `/btw` fork from a fresh request config. That fork path did not replay the persisted plugin app policy context, so an app configured with `allow_destructive_actions: "ask"` could lose its app-scoped `approvals_reviewer: "user"` boundary in the side conversation. Reusing the thread-level reviewer would not be equivalent: it could either miss the ask app or broaden approval routing for sibling apps.

## Why This Change Was Made

The side-question owner now merges `buildCodexPluginAppsConfigPatchFromPolicyContext(binding.pluginAppPolicyContext)` into the fork config, alongside the existing native-hook, runtime, network-proxy, sandbox, and base-reviewer fields. This uses the same canonical persisted-policy replay already used by thread start/resume, keeps the `"ask"` hard-cut naming from #98501, and does not introduce a compatibility path.

Focused regression coverage proves that an ask-mode app keeps app-scoped user review after the fork while sibling `true`, `false`, and `"auto"` apps retain their own policy and the top-level reviewer remains unchanged.

Contributor provenance: Kevin Lin (@kevinslin) authored the app-scoped approval design in #97327 and the `"ask"` hard cut in #98501. This follow-up preserves that boundary at the previously omitted side-fork owner.

AI-assisted: yes. Codex implemented the repair and completed a clean gpt-5.6-sol xhigh autoreview against the exact synced commit.

target.title: fix(ui): copy workspace file paths over plain HTTP
target.body:
Closes #98759

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users clicking **Copy path** in the Chat tab's Session Workspace files panel would get no copied path when the Control UI is served from a plain-HTTP context where `navigator.clipboard` is unavailable.

The workspace file row already routed the click back to the app-level workspace callback, but that callback used only the secure-context Clipboard API path. The existing Control UI clipboard helper already supports the legacy `execCommand("copy")` fallback used by other chat copy affordances.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes workspace path copying through the shared `copyToClipboard` helper instead of directly calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, keeping the workspace panel behavior aligned with the existing code-block copy fallback.

The E2E coverage now shares a plain-HTTP clipboard capture helper and adds a browser-level regression for the workspace Copy path button. This is a narrow Control UI fix; it does not change workspace file listing, file opening, Gateway RPCs, or clipboard UI state.

AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Users can copy Session Workspace file paths from the Chat tab even when accessing the Control UI over plain HTTP or another context where the async Clipboard API is not exposed.

Secure-context clipboard behavior remains unchanged because `copyToClipboard` still tries `navigator.clipboard.writeText` first.

## Evidence

Before source proof on current `upstream/main`: `ui/src/ui/app-render.ts` wired `copyChatWorkspacePath` to `globalThis.navigator?.clipboard?.writeText?.(filePath)`, so a missing Clipboard API made the Copy path click a no-op. The workspace rail was introduced in #92856; the reusable plain-HTTP clipboard fallback was added later in #93666 for code-block copying.

PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=<local chromium> node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts ui/src/ui/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts -t "copies a workspace file path"
```

target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.

target.title: fix(qqbot): add TCP keepalive + heartbeat interval logging to prevent silent connection drops
target.body:
### Problem

**Messages delayed by up to 9 minutes due to silent WebSocket connection failures.**

On 2026-05-04 07:13, a user sent a message via QQBot. The message was not received until 07:22:18 — **9 minutes of delay**. During this entire period, the OpenClaw gateway showed no errors, no reconnection attempts, and no heartbeat failures. The connection appeared healthy but was in fact dead.

**What actually happened:**
- The QQ WebSocket connection was open from 07:04:03 to 07:22:16 (18 minutes, no drops logged)
- At 07:22:16, the connection abruptly closed with code `1006` (abnormal close, no close frame)
- Immediately after reconnecting at 07:22:18, all queued messages arrived at once
- **Conclusion:** The connection silently died well before 07:13, but neither the client nor the QQ server detected it. Messages were buffered server-side and only delivered after the client reconnect.

**Why no detection?** The existing QQBot gateway implementation has two gaps:
1. **No TCP keepalive** — The `ws` library was instantiated without `setKeepAlive`, meaning the OS-level TCP connection is not probed. Network middleboxes (routers, NAT, firewalls) silently drop idle connections without sending RST/FIN.
2. **No heartbeat timeout detection** — If the server sends a `HEARTBEAT_ACK` on time, the client assumes the connection is healthy. But if the `HEARTBEAT_ACK` is lost in transit (because the underlying TCP path is dead), the client never notices. There is no timeout or ACK validation.

**Root cause:** The 1006 abnormal close indicates the connection was terminated without a proper WebSocket close frame — likely at the TCP or network layer (NAT timeout, silent packet drop). The client had no way to detect this before receiving a message, because there was no lower-level keepalive probe and no heartbeat ACK timeout.

### Solution

**Three changes in `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway-connection.ts`:**

#### 1. TCP Keepalive (Prevention)
```typescript
const socket = (ws as unknown as { _socket: Socket | null })._socket;
if (socket) {
  socket.setKeepAlive(true, 30_000);  // probe every 30s
  socket.setTimeout(60_000);          // 60s with no data → timeout
  socket.on("timeout", () => {
    log?.warn?.(`WebSocket socket timeout — closing and reconnecting`);
    ws.close();  // triggers existing reconnect flow
  });
}
```

- `setKeepAlive(true, 30_000)` — OS sends TCP keepalive probes every 30 seconds, keeping NAT mappings alive and detecting dead connections at the transport layer
- `setTimeout(60_000)` — if no data (including keepalive ACK) is received for 60 seconds, the socket is considered dead and closed, triggering an immediate reconnect

#### 2. Heartbeat Interval Logging (Debugging)
```typescript
const interval = d.heartbeat_interval;
this.ctx.log?.info(`Heartbeat interval: ${interval}ms (${(interval / 1000).toFixed(1)}s)`);
```

- Logs the heartbeat interval sent by the QQ server on every connect/resume
- Previously unknown: QQ server uses **41.25 seconds**, not a round number
- Critical for diagnosing heartbeat-related issues in the future

#### 3. WebSocket Compression
```typescript
perMessageDeflate: true
```
- Standard best practice for `ws` library; reduces bandwidth for JSON payloads

### Verification

- **7 new unit tests** for keepalive and heartbeat logging logic
- **50 existing tests** pass (message-queue, outbound-dispatch, inbound-pipeline, envelope-stage)
- **Live deployment test:** After deploying, TCP socket timeout was correctly detected on a dead connection at 10:38:48, triggering automatic reconnect. Heartbeat interval logged as `41250ms (41.3s)`.

### Expected Impact

- **Before:** Dead connections go undetected for minutes. Users see message delays of 5-10 minutes. Only a manual restart or the next server-side close triggers reconnect.
- **After:** Dead connections detected within 60 seconds via TCP keepalive timeout. Automatic reconnect restores message delivery. Heartbeat interval visible in logs for troubleshooting.

target.title: fix(matrix): add async shared-client stop helpers awaiting final persist
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: The synchronous `stopSharedClient`, `stopSharedClientForAccount`, and `stopSharedClientInstance` helpers in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/shared.ts` kick off the final crypto/sync persist via `MatrixClient.stop()` but return before it completes, so a process exit right after a stop can lose recently negotiated Olm/Megolm session keys.
- Why it matters: Lost crypto state shows up after restart as `InvalidMAC(MacError)` loops and repeated "Established new Olm sessions" against the same sender.
- What changed: Added async `stopSharedClientAsync`, `stopSharedClientForAccountAsync`, and `stopSharedClientInstanceAsync` that await `client.stopAndPersist()`. Marked the legacy synchronous helpers `@deprecated`. Re-exported the two account-scoped async helpers from the matrix barrel. Added three Vitest cases. Added one CHANGELOG line.
- What did NOT change: `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk.ts` was not touched. `MatrixClient.stop()` already triggers the final persist and `stopAndPersist()` already exists; the periodic 60s timer and the four crypto-event bindings at `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk/decrypt-bridge.ts:153-164` were already wired.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #76611 
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

Note: this PR narrowly fixes the synchronous stop-helper persistence defect from #76611 only. The event-driven crypto-state persist defect (`KeyBackupDecryptionKeyCached`, `RehydrationCompleted`, `DevicesUpdated`, `KeysChanged` not driving `persistIdbToDisk`) remains open and is not addressed here.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Sync helpers return `void` and call `client.stop()`, which assigns `stopPersistPromise` for the final IDB/sync flush but does not return it.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test pinned that shared-client teardown produces a settled persist promise; no `@deprecated` signal steered callers toward the existing async path.
- Contributing context: `releaseSharedClientInstance(client, "persist")` and `MatrixClient.stopAndPersist()` already exist as the safe path.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/shared.test.ts`
- Scenario: Each new async helper invokes `client.stopAndPersist()` exactly once on the targeted client(s) and does not call `client.stop()`.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The shared-client registry is the single chokepoint between callers and `MatrixClient`.
- Existing test that already covers this: None for the async-stop helpers.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin authors who deep-import `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client.ts` get three new async exports; legacy synchronous exports keep their current signatures.

## Diagram

N/A.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`

Net effect on security posture is positive: hardens the Matrix E2EE crypto-store shutdown path so recently negotiated session keys are durable across restarts when the new helpers are adopted.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11; fix is platform-agnostic.
- Runtime: Node 22.
- Integration: Matrix (`extensions/matrix`).

### Steps

1. Acquire a shared Matrix client through `resolveSharedMatrixClient` for an E2EE-enabled account.
2. Trigger a shutdown path that calls a synchronous `stopSharedClient*` helper and exits the process immediately.
3. Restart and observe whether incoming E2EE messages decrypt cleanly.

### Expected

- Recently negotiated Olm/Megolm sessions remain decryptable across restart.

### Actual (without this fix)

- Process exits before `stopPersistPromise` resolves; restart loses recent session keys, producing `InvalidMAC(MacError)` loops.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

Three Vitest cases added in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/shared.test.ts`. CI must run `pnpm test extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/shared.test.ts` and `pnpm test:changed`.

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Static review against the existing `releaseSharedClientInstance(client, "persist")` precedent at `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/shared.ts:295`. Verified the new helpers reuse `deleteSharedClientState` and `removeSharedClientInstance` with the same ordering as the existing async-release path. Verified the mock client in `shared.test.ts` exposes `stopAndPersist` without breaking the existing release-lease test.
- Edge cases checked: Concurrent acquire after a stop drops cleanly because state is removed before the awaited persist. `Promise.all` was chosen for `stopSharedClientAsync` to match the existing error semantics; inner persist work already catches errors with `.catch(noop)` at `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/sdk.ts:677-689`.
- What was not verified: Vitest was not executed in the authoring shell (no `pnpm`/`node` on PATH). The reporter's full prod symptom was not reproduced against a live homeserver.

## Review Conversations

- [x] Bot review conversations addressed in this PR will be replied to or resolved.
- [x] Only conversations that still need maintainer judgment will be left open.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: A future contributor copies a `@deprecated` synchronous helper into a new shutdown path despite the jsdoc warning.
  - Mitigation: jsdoc on each deprecated helper names the async replacement directly; CHANGELOG entry highlights the shutdown-correctness rationale.
- Risk: `Promise.all` in `stopSharedClientAsync` rejects on the first failing per-client persist.
  - Mitigation: Inner persist work already catches errors with `.catch(noop)`, so `stopAndPersist()` resolves under normal conditions; behavior matches `releaseSharedClientInstance(client, "persist")`.

target.title: fix(memory, builtin backend): eagerly preload session transcript listeners at gateway startup
target.body:
## Summary (scope narrowed to builtin backend per Codex review)

Eagerly preload `MemoryIndexManager` at gateway startup for every agent whose `agents.defaults.memorySearch.sources` (or per-agent overlay) includes `"sessions"`, **when using the builtin session-file backend**. This arms `ensureSessionListener()` before the first `sessionTranscriptUpdate` event fires, so `/reset` and `/new` archive emits actually land in the listener set and get indexed into `chunks` without the user having to run `openclaw memory index --force`.

## Why it was broken

`MemoryIndexManager` is lazy-loaded on the first `memory_search` tool call. If a user types `/reset` or `/new` before that first search, the builtin `archiveFileOnDisk` emit lands in an empty `SESSION_TRANSCRIPT_LISTENERS` set and is silently dropped, so the resulting `.jsonl.reset.<iso>` / `.jsonl.deleted.<iso>` archives never enter `chunks`. Only `memory index --force` recovers them (which is #76311 / #76452's escape hatch but is not a cold-start fix).

## Why builtin-only (Codex review response)

Thanks @clawsweeper for the P2 catch on the qmd path. The initial revision of this PR treated any successful `getActiveMemorySearchManager` result as listener-armed, but under the qmd backend that call returns the `FallbackMemoryManager` wrapper whose inner `MemoryIndexManager` is only constructed by `fallbackFactory`. So on qmd, merely obtaining the wrapper does NOT run `ensureSessionListener()`, and the cold-start race still drops `sessionTranscriptUpdate` emits.

Three options were on the table (per Codex):
1. Explicitly preload the builtin `MemoryIndexManager` listener owner even for qmd — requires reaching into the FallbackMemoryManager fallback slot.
2. Add qmd-native transcript event handling inside `qmd-manager.ts`.
3. **Narrow this PR to builtin-only and defer qmd to a follow-up.**

This revision takes **option 3**: added an explicit early-return guard `if (params.cfg.memory?.backend === "qmd") { ... return; }` at the top of `startGatewayMemorySessionListeners`, with a log line making the scope decision visible, plus a regression test (`skips preload entirely when memory.backend is qmd (Codex review scope guard)`). The changelog entry is also retitled `Memory/sessions (builtin backend):` and calls out the intentional qmd deferral.

## Independent verification (builtin only)

CarHer builtin-backend deployment (`carher-199` baseline). Three cold restarts, same container, identical `/reset` sequence:

| | pre-preload | post-preload |
|---|---|---|
| archive emit lands in listener set | ❌ dropped | ✅ captured |
| `chunks` delta after 30s | +0 | +41 |
| verified commit | `main @ 9a49d143c819` | `HEAD of this PR` |

## What is NOT included

- qmd backend session-listener arming (follow-up PR, tracked in body + changelog).
- Changes to `qmd-manager.ts` transcript event handling.
- Changes to `FallbackMemoryManager` fallback construction.

Refs #56131. AI-assisted.

## Summary

Adds a `<Warning>` callout to the Prometheus Quick Start clarifying that `plugins.allow` is **strict-mode** — when set, only listed plugins are eligible to load. The current Quick Start example shows `allow: ["diagnostics-prometheus"]` without warning that this disables every other configured plugin on a real running gateway.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was drafted with **Claude Code** (Anthropic's CLI agent).

- [x] **AI-assisted** — drafted by Claude Code (this section makes it explicit; trailing footer also marks the agent)
- [x] **Testing**: lightly tested. Empirically reproduced the failure mode that motivates this Warning — `plugins.allow: ["diagnostics-prometheus"]` dropped a 72-plugin running v2026.5.2 gateway to 9 enabled plugins; recovered via `openclaw config unset plugins.allow` + gateway restart. Did NOT build the docs site locally — render check left for CI / maintainer.
- [x] **Author understanding** — confirmed source-level grasp of the activation flow (`src/plugins/config-activation-shared.ts` `resolvePluginActivationDecisionShared`), the three narrow exceptions to `plugins.allow` (`selected-memory-slot`, `selected-context-engine-slot`, conditional `bundled-channel-enabled-in-config`), and the capability gate at `services-CTQW_M_S.js:15` that motivated cross-referenced #76628.
- [ ] **`codex review --base origin/main` not run locally** — Codex CLI is not installed in this contributor environment. Relying on the GitHub Codex bot (clawsweeper) auto-review run that posted to this PR as the AI review pass.
- [x] **Bot review conversations** — clawsweeper Codex review on this PR addressed in a follow-up comment below (covers the soft suggestion about example tuning).

## Why

Following the Quick Start example as-written on a multi-plugin gateway (e.g. one running `memory-core`, `active-memory`, `memory-wiki`, `telegram`, etc.) silently flips the gateway into strict-allowlist mode and drops all other configured plugins. On a 71-plugin running gateway (mid-sized self-hosted setup), the example dropped the enabled-plugin count from 72 to **9** — including critical plugins like `memory-core`, `active-memory`, and the configured Telegram channel — until rolled back via `openclaw config unset plugins.allow`.

The warning surface for this is misleading in two ways:

1. The startup log line `[plugins] plugins.allow is empty; discovered non-bundled plugins may auto-load: <id>. Set plugins.allow to explicit trusted ids.` *implies* setting `plugins.allow` is the right next step. It isn't, in the general case.
2. The schema description for `plugins.allow` is correct (*"when set, only listed plugins are eligible to load"*), but the Quick Start snippet doesn't reproduce that semantics in user-visible documentation.

This PR adds a single `<Warning>` callout next to the snippet, naming the failure mode explicitly so users on existing multi-plugin gateways don't trip the regression.

## Cross-references

- **#75575** (open) — *Honor `plugins.allow` on runtime provider paths (currently force-loaded) — propose `plugins.bundledMode` opt-in*. Same family of `plugins.allow` semantic confusion. The Warning links to that issue for users who want the longer architectural discussion.
- **#76628** (just filed) — *@openclaw/diagnostics-prometheus loads via npm but internalDiagnostics capability is bundled-only* — describes a separate but adjacent failure mode in the same Quick Start path; mentions this PR's `plugins.allow` finding as one of the empirical investigations along the way.

## Scope

- Single-file doc change: `docs/gateway/prometheus.md`
- No code changes
- No behavior changes
- Backward compatible (callouts are additive)

## Test plan

- [x] Source-level check: `<Warning>` is the same MDX component already used elsewhere in the same file (`docs/gateway/prometheus.md:19-21`), so no new component dependencies. Indentation matches the surrounding `<Step>` / `<Tabs>` block.
- [ ] Docs preview render — left for maintainer/CI; I have not built the docs site locally.
- [x] Empirically reproduced the regression that this Warning describes (multi-plugin gateway dropping from 72 → 9 enabled plugins after applying the existing snippet, fully recovered by `openclaw config unset plugins.allow` + restart). See **#76628** for the full reproduction.

target.title: fix(zalouser): split messages at line boundaries instead of mid-word
target.body:
## TL;DR

Long bot responses were split mid-word because the default chunk mode cut at exactly 2000 characters with no regard for word or sentence boundaries.

---

## Problem

`DEFAULT_TEXT_CHUNK_MODE = "length"` cuts the outgoing message at exactly the 2000-character limit regardless of whether that lands in the middle of a word. In practice this was observed as a Vietnamese word like "lên" arriving as two separate messages — "lê" followed by "n" — which is unreadable.

The `"newline"` chunk mode already exists in the codebase and correctly breaks at paragraph boundaries → single newlines → whitespace → hard cut (as a last resort). It was never set as the default, so callers that did not explicitly pass `textChunkMode: "newline"` got the hard-cut behavior.

---

## Invariant

> When a message is split into chunks, each chunk boundary must fall at a natural break (paragraph, newline, or whitespace) unless no such break exists within the limit window.

---

## What this PR does

- Changes `DEFAULT_TEXT_CHUNK_MODE` from `"length"` to `"newline"` in `send.ts`
- Adds one regression test: a message with a paragraph break inside the 2000-char window is split at the break, not at position 2000

---

## Why this matters

- **User impact**: Words arrived split across two Zalo messages, making bot responses unreadable in long replies.
- **System impact**: The hard-cut behavior never had a use case — `"newline"` falls back to a hard cut when no natural break exists, so it is strictly better for all inputs.

---

## Safety

- The `splitTextRangesByPreferredBreaks` function (used by `"newline"` mode) falls back to a hard cut when no natural break point is found, so behavior for texts with no whitespace is unchanged.
- All existing tests pass unchanged: they use continuous character strings with no natural break points, which fall through to the same hard-cut behavior as before.
- No change to any other logic.

---

## Test plan

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/zalouser/src/send.test.ts
```

- [x] All existing tests pass (13)
- [x] New test: paragraph break within window → split at break, not at position 2000

target.title: fix(zalouser): surface send errors and recover from oversized style payloads
target.body:
## TL;DR

Zalo delivery failures were completely invisible: the monitor never checked send results, error codes were lost, and messages silently disappeared when styled payloads exceeded Zalo's size limit.

---

## Problem

Three compounding gaps caused messages to vanish without any log trace:

1. `sendZaloTextMessage` caught errors but discarded the numeric `error_code` from Zalo's response — callers could not distinguish a transient network error from a Zalo-specific rejection.
2. The `sendText` and `sendMedia` callbacks in the monitor called `sendMessageZalouser` without checking the returned result, so `ok=false` responses were silently dropped.
3. Zalo rejects messages with `error_code=112` when the combined params payload (message text + `textProperties` JSON for styling) exceeds its server-side size limit. Empirically: a ~1420-char Vietnamese message combined with 56+ style ranges (~1871 chars of JSON) triggers this. The message was never delivered and no error appeared in logs.

---

## Invariant

> When Zalo rejects a styled message with error code 112, the message text must still be delivered (without styles), and the failure must be logged if delivery ultimately fails.

---

## What this PR does

- Adds `errorCode?: number` to `ZaloSendResult` so callers can branch on specific Zalo error codes
- Enhances `toErrorMessage` to include the numeric code in the string so it appears in logs
- Extracts the numeric error code from caught errors in `sendZaloTextMessage` and attaches it to the result
- Adds a retry-without-styles path in `sendMessageZalouser` on error code 112: if the styled send fails with 112, the message is re-sent as plain text
- Makes `sendText` and `sendMedia` in the monitor check `result.ok` and emit a structured error log when delivery fails

---

## Why this matters

- **User impact**: Long bot responses with markdown formatting silently failed to reach Zalo users. The bot appeared to respond on the web UI but nothing arrived in the chat.
- **System impact**: Failures were completely unobservable — no logs, no error propagation — making debugging impossible without adding instrumentation manually.

---

## Safety

- No change to message delivery path when everything succeeds
- The retry only triggers on the specific error code 112 with styled content; all other errors are forwarded unchanged
- Existing tests unchanged; 3 new regression tests added

---

## Test plan

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/zalouser/src/send.test.ts
```

- [x] All existing tests pass (13)
- [x] New test: retries without styles on error code 112
- [x] New test: propagates error when retry also fails
- [x] New test: does not retry when there are no styles
